# Target C model: computing our own "C_best" deterministically

The arena scores a deal by `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`. `C_best` is hidden during a case, so the agent needs its **own estimate of C_best** to know where to anchor and when it is close enough. This note explains how we compute it, and how accurate it was in the sandbox.

Related: [[Engine-Prototype]] · [[Arena-Workflow-and-Learnings]] · [[Research-Negotiation-Techniques]] · [[../Progress/Runs/2026-10-10-sandbox-engine-runs|Sandbox engine runs]]
Code: `~/Documents/EHL-Hackathon-code/starter-kit/proto/target.py`

## The idea

The brief defines `C_best` as *the best package any supplier would ever accept, with every valid lever applied*. A supplier never sells below its **cost floor**. The kit already contains the function that turns any package into the **cash the supplier really receives per unit**: `arena_kit.cost.supplier_value()`. It accounts for payment days (at the supplier's cost of money), the start date (units

So, once we have an estimate of the supplier's floor:

```
for every lever combination allowed by the case (term_options: payment, contract, start date, lead time, Incoterm):
    p*  = the unit price where supplier_value(package at p*) == floor      (bisection)
    C*  = total_cost(package at p*)                                         (the published C)
    skip packages that break a must-have
    strategic goals (stabilise / secure_supply): also try prices above p*, because squeezing
    the supplier below its sustainable margin adds a relationship cost to C
C_target = min over all packages and all suppliers, and our alternative (if any)
```

Two refinements we needed:
- **Lead times faster than the supplier's standard and our need are excluded.** They gain us nothing (C only charges days *beyond* our need) but cost the supplier overtime, which `supplier_value` does not see.
- **Price for a given C (for equal-C term sheets).** With a relationship term, C is *not* monotone in price: it first falls (we stop squeezing) and then rises. `price_for_c` finds the cheapest price by ternary search and solves only on the rising side.

## Estimating the floor from in-game evidence (no hindsight)

| Situation | Estimate | Source in the case |
|---|---|---|
| Price increase, strategic goal (D01) | `full_cost = current_price / (1 + sustainable_margin) × (1 + Σ share × index move)`: the supplier was healthy at today's price, and its cost moved only by the drivers it cites | Case file (`current_unit_price`, `sustainable_margin_pct`) + supplier letter ("WAGES-METAL rose 3.1 % … is 28 % of our cost") |
| Supplier sent a cost breakdown (D02, J1) | `floor = material + wages + conversion` (excluding overhead and profit) | The cost-breakdown XLSX, which you get by asking in round 1 |
| Supplier states its material share (D02, C1) | `floor = material €/unit (from another supplier's breakdown) / material share` | "Material accounts for about 45 % of our cost" |
| Nothing yet | `floor = 85 % of the lowest opening price` | Opening quotes |

The estimate is recomputed after round 1, once the documents have arrived.

## How accurate was it?

After each sandbox case the result reveals the true `c_best`, so we can grade the estimator:

| Case | Our C_target | True c_best | Error | Implied floor (back-solved) | Our floor estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D01 (foundry, +8.8 %) | €397,779 | €408,624 | **−2.7 %** (too aggressive) | full cost ≈ €48.0 | €47.14 |
| D02 prior (before documents) | €168,427 | €156,739 | +7.5 % (too soft) | n/a | 85 % of €16.00 = €13.60 |
| D02 after round-1 documents | €155,933 | €156,739 | **−0.5 %** | ≈ €12.4–12.5 | C1: 5.56 / 0.45 = **€12.36** |

The best packages implied by the model:
- **D01:** 24 months, start delayed to Feb–Apr 2027, 30 days payment, price about €47.6–49.1. The supplier is left a little below its 4 % margin.
- **D02:** the Polish supplier (C1), 14 days payment, 35 days lead time, DAP or FCA, about €12.8.

## Limits and open questions

- The D01 estimate assumes the supplier earned exactly the sustainable margin at the old price. The truth was about 2 % higher. A better prior might use the price history (`price_conditions`) or a should-cost (`cost:` IDs) when one exists.
- We guessed each supplier's cost of money from its persona (cash-short job shop 20 %, family foundry 10 %, growing exporter 12 %). In the cases we checked, `C_target` was barely sensitive to this.
- The model knows nothing about a supplier's **behaviour**, only its economics. Knowing the target precisely did **not** by itself get us there. See [[Engine-Prototype]] and the runs note for what actually moved suppliers.
- Hosted practice cases have real data packages (`should_cost`, `cost_drivers`, index series), so the floor can be estimated much better there. Port the estimator to use `cost:` and `idx:` data.

+**Context.** RxV00's engine (`proto/engine.py`, not in a repo yet; notes in the EHL-Hackathon vault:

+practice `6ab56f8485cbf9cb` …) and ported what made the difference. No practice quota used.
+1. **Target from the supplier's floor, ask 3 % below it.** Floor = our should-cost; for a price letter today's price
+   less a sustainable margin, moved by the drivers the supplier itself cites ("WAGES-METAL rose 3.1 % … is 28 % of
+   our cost"); else 85 % of the lowest quote. Strategic goals: the price where the relationship charge starts.
+   D01: floor 47.14, target 48.04 (24 months, April start, 30 days) - the engine's own numbers.
+2. **Concede early** (e = 2) from the target towards the supplier's *standing* offer, meeting it at round 4;
+   round 0 asks the target; never retreat.
+3. **Hold** up to 2 rounds while the supplier still gives ≥ 0.5 %.
+4. **Alternatives:** only a supplier's first sheet can be accepted - a better alternative is sent back exactly
+   ("we take your alternative exactly as offered") and accepted on `agreed`.
+5. **Cite the case's references even when we cannot look them up** (sandbox, hidden cases) - by ID, no figure:
+   the arena checks them itself ("it holds and we took it into account").
+6. **Volume commitment** ("we commit bindingly to N a year … our entire need, all of it with you"), thanks for the
+   supplier's movement, closing questions ("How could we close the remaining gap today?").
+7. **Not taken:** pushing after a final offer in a single-supplier case - practice P10: the push made the
+   supplier walk (no deal). We push once only with a fallback offer.
+**Result on the hosted sandbox (2 plays per case)**
+| First port, curve off by one round (`enginelearn`) | 0.57 | 0.39 | 47.9 |
+The messages alone are worth ~+9 points; the floor-based target and early concession another ~+13.
+**Per case type** (`analysis.BOULWARE_TYPES`): the engine approach for price increases, renewals, RFQs and bundles
+(it won P01-P05 in practice); our first curve for raw material, capacity and quality (our orchestra won P08, P10,
+P11, P18). `ORCH_CURVE=engine|boulware` forces one for every case. **Untested on practice suppliers** (no quota
+today): the first practice pass should be one per case type, before Sunday's final.
+**Also learned on the way** (our own logs, `scripts/supplier_moves.py`, `scripts/what_moves_them.py`): a supplier's
+*first* counter barely depends on our ask (within-supplier slope 0.08); it does not move without a move from us

entries.name: EnterWorktree
entries.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

content.content:
# proto: Tugra's buyer engine (branch `tugra`)

A deterministic negotiation engine: **code picks every number, templates write the e-mail** (no LLM needed). It plays
any case of the arena (sandbox, practice, final). The tactics were found by an evolutionary search on the sandbox,
checked on all 10 hosted practice cases, and improved with ideas from the orchestra and a teammate's D02 replay.

Full write-up in the shared Obsidian vault (RxV00/EHL-Hackathon): `Progress/Experiment-Log.md` (every change and its
measured effect), `App/Engine-Prototype.md` (architecture + changelog), `App/Target-C-Model.md`,
`Progress/Practice-Run-A-Findings.md`, `Progress/Teammate-Findings-Comparison.md`.

## Results

| Algorithm | D01 (sandbox) | D02 (sandbox, mean of 3) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| naive kit agent | 0.20 | – | |
| A (search winner) | 0.979 | 0.640 | practice: mean 0.557 over 10 cases; P02 0.684 and P04 0.874 were case records |
| A2 (+ fixes from practice) | 0.979 | 0.626 | safe push, bottleneck anchor, say-fixed, meet supplier terms, RFQ in-flight guard |
| **A3 (+ staggered RFQ opening)** | **0.979** | **0.728** (0.740, 0.740, 0.703) | **main algorithm**; the D02 friend replay scored 0.661 |

## Run

From `starter-kit/` (keys in the root `.env`, as in the rest of the repo; `load_env()` reads `.env` in the working
directory, so copy or symlink it if needed):

```bash
# sandbox (free): A3 once on D01, three times on D02 (D02 is noisy)
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/variants.py --cases case:D01:1 case:D02:3 --variants A3

# hosted practice (COSTS QUOTA - ask the team first): facts and floors from the data package
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/variants.py --practice --cases case:P05:1 --variants A3

# one case, any Config as JSON
ENGINE_CFG='{"e": 2, "T": 4, "rfq_stagger": true}' PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/engine.py case:D02

# negotiate by hand (interactive)
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/chat.py case:D01

# after a kill: close only the sessions this engine opened (never teammates' sessions)
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/cleanup.py proto/runs/variants
```

## How A3 negotiates

1. **Target C** (`target.py`): for every allowed combination of levers, the price where the supplier's cash value
   (`cost.supplier_value`) equals its estimated cost floor, costed with the published C; the minimum is our own
   C_best estimate. Floors come from in-game evidence: should-cost (capped so the opening keeps a sustainable
   margin), the supplier's cost breakdown, cost drivers × index moves.
2. **First ask:** 3 % beyond that target; for `secure_supply` (bottleneck) at most 3 % below the opening.
3. **Every message:** 2 term sheets of equal cost to us that differ in the levers the supplier values; 2 new
   verified facts (only *falling* indices); answers to its questions (volume, fixed terms); in an RFQ the best
   rival offer by ID; warm tone. If it keeps insisting on a term we never offered (e.g. its index clause), one
   sheet takes that term at equal cost to us.
4. **Concession:** visible from round 1 (curve e=2), planned over 4 rounds, aimed at its current offer.
5. **RFQ:** one worker per supplier, each on its own 60-second clock; **staggered opening**: the cheapest quote
   first, the others opened citing its fresh reply; never close while a supplier is untouched or a reply is in flight.
6. **Closing:** accept at our next goal (one extra round if it still moves > 0.5 %); after a final offer push 2 × 1 %
   **only when a rival's offer backs us up**; mirror an alternative sheet back before accepting it; close
   `max(90 s, slowest round + 15 s)` before a wave cap; never above the supplier's own price, never a broken must-have.

"""Research-driven buyer prototype: code picks every number, templates write the e-mail.

    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/engine.py case:D01 case:D02            # default Config
    ENGINE_CFG='{"e": 2, "T": 4}' PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/engine.py case:D02

Per round: target C (proto.target) -> concession curve on C -> equal-C term sheets (MESO) ->
templated e-mail (facts, answers, rival offer, question) -> replies -> acceptance rule.
Every tactic is a field of Config, so proto/search.py can try many variants in parallel.
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError, complete_offer, must_haves_ok, total_cost
from arena_kit.cli import load_env
from arena_kit.cost import supplier_value
from arena_kit.docs import read_document, standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import ENDED

from proto.target import lever_grid, price_for_c, target

LOG_DIR = Path("proto/runs")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    e: float = 1.0  # concession curve exponent: <1 firm until late, 1 linear, >1 concede early
    T: int = 4  # rounds over which our goal travels from the target to the reference offer
    toward: str = "standing"  # curve end: "standing" (best standing offer) or "open" (best opening quote)
    anchor: float = 0.0  # first goal = target x (1 + anchor); negative = more aggressive
    holds: int = 1  # extra rounds at an unchanged goal while the supplier still gives > hold_gave
    hold_gave: float = 0.01  # share of C the supplier must have given last round to earn a hold
    push: str = "all"  # after a final offer: "all", "rfq" (only with a fallback offer) or "off"
    pushes: int = 1  # how many small asks after a final offer
    push_pct: float = 0.015  # size of each ask below its standing price
    meso_n: int = 3  # term sheets per message (1-3)
    pick: str = "diverse"  # which packages: "diverse" or "near" (closest to the supplier's own levers)
    facts: int = 1  # new citable facts per message
    rival: bool = True  # RFQ: tell each supplier the rival's standing offer (ID + attachment)
    calc: bool = True  # attach our calculation from the supplier's own breakdown when asked
    volume: bool = True  # answer "which volume can you commit to?"
    tone: str = "warm"  # "warm" or "brief"
    max_rounds: int = 8
    # ideas from the teammates' practice runs (Team-Knowledge, 2026-10-10)
    anchor_mode: str = "target"  # "target": open at our C_target; "opening": per-goal % below the opening quote
    long_contract: bool = False  # longest contract_months >= horizon in every sheet (free for us, valued by suppliers)
    say_fixed: bool = False  # when a supplier asks for a fixed term, say it is fixed in this enquiry
    rfq_bar: bool = False  # RFQ: an early "agreed" is the bar for one more rival round, not the deal
    rfq_hold: bool = False  # RFQ: a short no-sheet e-mail keeps a final-offer supplier's clock alive
    news: bool = False  # cite news rows about the supplier (practice/final data only)
    # fixes from practice run A (Progress/Practice-Run-A-Findings)
    bottleneck_anchor: float = 0.0  # secure_supply: first ask at least opening x (1 - this); 0 = off
    meet_fields: bool = False  # one package takes the supplier's value for a term it set (e.g. its index clause)
    # from the friend's D02 replay e843da929222686e (0.661)
    rfq_stagger: bool = False  # RFQ: open with the cheapest quote first, then the others citing its fresh reply
    breakdown_arg: bool = False  # quote the supplier's own cost breakdown back (material + labour + conversion)
    volume_framing: bool = False  # monthly baseline, "quote the trade-off for a larger lot", no-overtime lead time

"""Named algorithms (our search winner + the teammates' ideas) and a parallel runner.

    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/variants.py --cases case:D01:1 case:D02:3 --variants A B C D
    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/variants.py --practice --cases case:P05:1 --variants A D   # costs quota!

`case:D02:3` plays each variant 3 times on D02 (D02 is noisy, D01 is deterministic).
Results: proto/runs/variants/results.jsonl; summary printed per variant and case.
"""

import argparse
import json
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from dataclasses import asdict, replace
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError
from arena_kit.cli import load_env

import proto.engine as eng
from proto.engine import Config

OUT = Path("proto/runs/variants")

# A: the tactic search's winner (gen 1 best mean, with 2 term sheets - best on both cases in the effect table)
A = Config(e=2.0, anchor=-0.03, hold_gave=0.005, pushes=2, push_pct=0.01, facts=2, calc=False, meso_n=2)
VARIANTS = {
    "A": ("Search best", A),
    "B": ("A + teammates' opening-based anchors", replace(A, anchor_mode="opening")),
    "C": ("A + RFQ: agreement as bar, hold e-mail", replace(A, rfq_bar=True, rfq_hold=True)),
    "D": ("A + all teammate ideas", replace(A, anchor_mode="opening", rfq_bar=True, rfq_hold=True,
                                           long_contract=True, say_fixed=True, news=True)),
    "E": ("A + say-fixed + long contract (practice levers only)", replace(A, long_contract=True, say_fixed=True)),
    # A2: fixes from practice run A (Progress/Practice-Run-A-Findings)
    "A2": ("A + practice fixes: safe push, bottleneck anchor, say-fixed, meet fields",
           replace(A, push="rfq", bottleneck_anchor=0.03, say_fixed=True, meet_fields=True)),
    # from the friend's D02 replay e843da929222686e (0.661)
    "F": ("A2 + staggered RFQ opening", replace(VARIANTS_A2 := replace(A, push="rfq", bottleneck_anchor=0.03,
          say_fixed=True, meet_fields=True), rfq_stagger=True)),
    "G": ("A2 + breakdown argument + volume framing", replace(VARIANTS_A2, breakdown_arg=True, volume_framing=True)),
    "H": ("A2 + all three friend ideas", replace(VARIANTS_A2, rfq_stagger=True, breakdown_arg=True, volume_framing=True)),
    "A3": ("Main algorithm: A2 + staggered RFQ opening (= F)", replace(VARIANTS_A2, rfq_stagger=True)),
    "A2all": ("A2 but pushing after every final offer (to price the safety)",
              replace(A, push="all", bottleneck_anchor=0.03, say_fixed=True, meet_fields=True)),
}


def run_one(client, name, cfg, case, rep, practice):
    if practice:
        from proto.practice import PracticeNegotiator
        eng.Negotiator = PracticeNegotiator
    for attempt in range(6):
        try:
            sid, res = eng.play(case, cfg, client=client, log_dir=OUT / name, quiet=True)
            break
        except ArenaError as e:  # e.g. 429 too many open sessions: wait for a slot
            time.sleep(10 * (attempt + 1))
    else:
        sid, res = None, {"score": None, "error": "could not open a session"}
    row = {"variant": name, "case": case, "rep": rep, "session": sid, "cfg": asdict(cfg), "score": res.get("score"),
           "c_deal": res.get("c_deal"), "c_best": res.get("c_best"), "terms": res.get("terms"), "error": res.get("error")}
    with open(OUT / "results.jsonl", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    return row


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--cases", nargs="+", default=["case:D01:1", "case:D02:3"])
    ap.add_argument("--variants", nargs="+", default=list(VARIANTS))
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--practice", action="store_true", help="data-package facts/floors (costs practice quota!)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    load_env()
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    client = ArenaClient()
    jobs = []
    for spec in a.cases:
        case, _, n = spec.rpartition(":") if spec.count(":") == 2 else (spec, None, "1")
        for rep in range(int(n)):
            for v in a.variants:
                jobs.append((v, VARIANTS[v][1], case, rep))
    print(f"{len(jobs)} sessions, {a.workers} at a time", flush=True)
    rows = []
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(a.workers) as ex:
        futs = [ex.submit(run_one, client, v, cfg, case, rep, a.practice) for v, cfg, case, rep in jobs]
        for i, f in enumerate(as_completed(futs), 1):
            r = f.result()
            rows.append(r)
            print(f"  [{i}/{len(jobs)}] {r['variant']} {r['case']} rep{r['rep']} score={r['score']} err={r['error']}", flush=True)
    table = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for r in rows:
        table[r["variant"]][r["case"]].append(r["score"] if r["score"] is not None else 0.0)
    cases = sorted({r["case"] for r in rows})
    print("\nvariant | " + " | ".join(cases))
    for v in a.variants:
        cells = []
        for c in cases:
            s = table[v][c]
            cells.append(f"{sum(s) / len(s):.3f} {[round(x, 3) for x in s]}" if s else "-")
        print(f"{v} {VARIANTS[v][0]} | " + " | ".join(cells))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"""Walk away from sessions OUR search opened and never finished (e.g. after a kill).
Never touches any other session on the team key."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient
from arena_kit.cli import load_env

d = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "proto/runs/search")
opened = set((d / "opened.txt").read_text().split()) if (d / "opened.txt").exists() else set()
closed = set((d / "closed.txt").read_text().split()) if (d / "closed.txt").exists() else set()
load_env()
c = ArenaClient()
for sid in sorted(opened - closed):
    st = c.session(sid)
    if st.get("status") == "ended":
        continue
    c.send_message(sid, list(st["threads"])[0], {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}})
    print("closed our session", sid)

"""The Live Final with Tugra's engine: wait for each wave, play its cases in parallel within the wave's cap.

    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/final.py                                   # Live Final: start before wave 1
    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/final.py --rehearse case:D01 case:D02      # free dress rehearsal (sandbox)
    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/final.py --rehearse case:D01 case:D02 -n 2 --cap 240   # tight cap, 4 sessions

Every case is played with algorithm A3 (proto/variants.py) through the data-package adapter (proto/practice.py:
facts and floors from the data, the Sunday release included). ENGINE_CFG='{"e": 2}' overrides single settings.
What it keeps from the rules: one session per case (after a restart it resumes ours), at most 10 open sessions,
the wave's cap followed from `seconds_left` on every poll (the host may extend a wave), and it never reads
/v1/events, /screen, /leaderboard or /results. A broken case never stops the others or the runner.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import statistics
import sys
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import asdict, replace
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError
from arena_kit.cli import load_env

import proto.engine as eng
from proto.practice import PracticeNegotiator
from proto.variants import VARIANTS

LOG = Path("proto/runs/final")
POLL_S = 5.0
_write = threading.Lock()


def config():
    """A3, with single settings overridden by ENGINE_CFG (JSON)."""
    return replace(VARIANTS["A3"][1], **json.loads(os.environ.get("ENGINE_CFG", "{}")))


def say(text):
    print(f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} {text}", flush=True)


def one(client, case, cfg, deadline, log_dir):
    """Play one case to its end. Returns a result row; never raises."""
    cid, t0 = case["case_id"], time.time()
    row = {"case": cid, "wave": case.get("wave"), "theme": case.get("theme"), "started": time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")}
    try:
        sid, res = eng.play(cid, cfg, client=client, log_dir=log_dir, quiet=True, deadline=deadline, case=case)
        keep = ("deal", "score", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "c_alt", "end_reason", "supplier_id", "error")
        row.update(session=sid, **{k: res.get(k) for k in keep if k in res})
    except Exception as e:  # e.g. the session could not be opened at all
        row["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]
    cap = deadline() if callable(deadline) else deadline
    row.update(seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 1), left_at_close=round(cap - time.time(), 1) if cap else None)
    with _write, open(LOG / "results.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, default=str) + "\n")
    score = row.get("score")
    say(f"{cid} (wave {row['wave']}): {'deal' if row.get('deal') else 'no deal'}, score {score}, "
        f"{row['seconds']} s, {row['left_at_close']} s before the cap {row.get('error') or ''}")
    return row


def summary(rows):
    waves = {}
    for r in rows:
        waves.setdefault(r.get("wave"), []).append(r.get("score") or 0.0)
    for w, s in sorted(waves.items(), key=lambda kv: str(kv[0])):
        deals = sum(bool(r.get("deal")) for r in rows if r.get("wave") == w)
        say(f"wave {w}: {len(s)} cases, {deals} deals, {100 * statistics.mean(s):.1f} points (our own record)")

def _estimate(self):
        b = self.b
        lowest_open = min((t.sheets[0]["terms"]["unit_price"] for t in self.threads.values() if t.sheets), default=None)
        texts = {s: " ".join((m.get("body") or "") + " " + " ".join(a.get("text") or "" for a in m.get("attachments") or [])
                             for m in t.events if m.get("from") != "buyer") for s, t in self.threads.items()}
        material = None  # material cost per unit from any breakdown we hold (same bar for every supplier)
        for txt in texts.values():
            if m := re.search(r"BAR-\S+ \(material[^|]*\| ([\d.]+)", txt):
                material = float(m.group(1))
        for s, t in self.threads.items():
            std = {**t.std, **self.case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
            std.setdefault("payment_days", b["reference_payment_days"])
            std.setdefault("incoterm", max(b["freight_eur_per_unit"], key=b["freight_eur_per_unit"].get))
            est = {"standard": std, "interest_rate": CASH_RATE.get(s, 0.10), "basis": None}
            txt = texts[s]
            if b.get("current_unit_price") and self.relationship:
                # healthy at today's price (sustainable margin), cost moved only by the drivers it cites
                drift = sum(float(mv) * float(sh) / 1e4 for _, mv, sh in
                            re.findall(r"(\S+) rose ([\d.]+) % in twelve months and is (\d+) % of our cost", txt))
                full = b["current_unit_price"] / (1 + b["sustainable_margin_pct"] / 100) * (1 + drift)
                est.update(full_cost=round(full, 2), floor=round(full, 2), basis=f"current price / (1+margin) x (1+{drift:.4f})")
            elif bd := BREAKDOWN.search(txt):
                est.update(floor=round(sum(float(x) for x in bd.groups()), 2), basis="own cost breakdown: material + wages + conversion")
            elif material and (sh := re.search(r"Material accounts for about (\d+) %", txt)):
                est.update(floor=round(material / (int(sh.group(1)) / 100), 2), basis=f"material {material} / {sh.group(1)} % share")
            elif lowest_open:
                est.update(floor=round(0.85 * lowest_open, 2), basis="prior: 85 % of the lowest opening price")
            t.est = est
        rows = target(self.case, {s: t.est for s, t in self.threads.items() if t.est.get("floor")})
        self.target_c, self.target_sup, self.target_terms = rows[0] if rows else (float("inf"), None, None)
        self.note("target", c_target=self.target_c, supplier=self.target_sup, terms=self.target_terms,
                  floors={s: (t.est.get("floor"), t.est.get("basis")) for s, t in self.threads.items()})

    # ---------- offers ----------
    def best_standing(self):

content.thinking: I found that the sandbox is caching supplier replies, so repeated deterministic runs (like my D02 ×3 results) aren't truly independent samples and the tight-cap test wasn't actually exercised. I'll add a `--fresh` flag that uniquely tags each e-mail per session to force new replies, then rerun the tight-cap test with real latency.

content.thinking: A4 consistently outperforms and is steadier than A3 across runs, confirming it as the better base; however, the 429 errors reveal a bug where the runner gives up entirely if all session slots are briefly full instead of retrying. I'll now fix the runner to wait for a free slot when time permits, along with a test for this case.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='proto/final.py'
s=open(p).read()
old='''    cid, t0 = case["case_id"], time.time()
    row = {"case": cid, "wave": case.get("wave"), "theme": case.get("theme"), "started": time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")}
    try:
        sid, res = eng.play(cid, cfg, client=client, log_dir=log_dir, quiet=True, deadline=deadline, case=case)
        keep = ("deal", "score", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "c_alt", "end_reason", "supplier_id", "error")
        row.update(session=sid, **{k: res.get(k) for k in keep if k in res})
    except Exception as e:  # e.g. the session could not be opened at all
        row["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]
    cap = deadline() if callable(deadline) else deadline'''
new='''    cid, t0 = case["case_id"], time.time()
    row = {"case": cid, "wave": case.get("wave"), "theme": case.get("theme"), "started": time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")}
    while True:
        cap = deadline() if callable(deadline) else deadline
        try:
            sid, res = eng.play(cid, cfg, client=client, log_dir=log_dir, quiet=True, deadline=deadline, case=case)
            keep = ("deal", "score", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "c_alt", "end_reason", "supplier_id", "error")
            row.update(session=sid, **{k: res.get(k) for k in keep if k in res})
        except ArenaError as e:  # 429: the key's 10 open sessions are in use; wait for a slot while time is left
            if e.status == 429 and (cap is None or cap - time.time() > OPEN_MIN_S):
                say(f"{cid}: no free session slot yet ({e.detail}); retrying in {RETRY_S:.0f} s")
                time.sleep(RETRY_S)
                continue
            row["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]
        except Exception as e:  # e.g. the session could not be opened at all
            row["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]
        break
    cap = deadline() if callable(deadline) else deadline'''
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
old='''POLL_S = 5.0
'''
new='''POLL_S = 5.0
RETRY_S, OPEN_MIN_S = 5.0, 60  # no free session slot: retry every 5 s while more than 60 s of the wave are left
'''
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='tests/test_proto_final.py'
s=open(p).read()
s += '''

def test_a_full_key_is_waited_out_not_given_up(fast, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(final, "RETRY_S", 0.01)
    tries = []

    def busy_then_free(cid, cfg, client=None, log_dir=None, quiet=False, deadline=None, case=None):
        tries.append(cid)
        if len(tries) < 3:
            raise ArenaError(429, "at most 10 open sessions per key")
        return "S1", {"deal": True, "score": 0.7}

    monkeypatch.setattr(final.eng, "play", busy_then_free)
    row = final.one(None, case("case:H1", 1, True, 480), final.config(), lambda: time.time() + 480, final.LOG)
    assert len(tries) == 3 and row["score"] == 0.7 and "error" not in row
    tries.clear()  # with too little time left it stops trying: the case scores its alternative
    row = final.one(None, case("case:H1", 1, True, 30), final.config(), lambda: time.time() + 30, final.LOG)
    assert len(tries) == 1 and "429" in row["error"]
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
uv run ruff check proto/final.py tests/test_proto_final.py && uv run ruff format proto/final.py tests/test_proto_final.py | tail -1 && uv run pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -1

# Sandbox results: Tugra's engine (branch `tugra`), A3 → A4, 2026-10-10 evening

All runs on the free hosted sandbox (D01 price increase, 1 supplier, `stabilise`; D02 RFQ, 2 suppliers, `leverage`).
No practice sessions used. Changes are in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/tugra`, **not committed yet**.

## Headline

| Config | How it plays | D01 | D02 | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A3 (Tugra's main) | hand-written sandbox facts | 0.979 | 0.740 | 0.860 |
| A3 | **data adapter = how the Live Final plays every case** | 0.894 (0.889, 0.905, 0.889) | 0.613 (0.640, 0.619, 0.492, 0.701) | 0.754 |
| **A4 (new)** | **data adapter** | **0.987** (0.969–0.996, 7 plays) | **0.684** (0.661–0.703, 10 plays) | **0.836** |

**A4 recovers most of what the hand-written facts were worth (+0.08 mean over A3 in the final's code path), with no
case-specific knowledge,** and its D02 is much steadier: 0.66–0.70 vs A3's 0.49–0.70.

## What changed (all on branch `tugra`)

1. **A4 = A3 + two settings that only act where our data knows nothing** (new suppliers or parts, the sandbox):
   - `game_evidence`: the supplier's floor from what it told us: the cost drivers it cites in its letter, its
     cost breakdown (after round 1), its material share. Before, the adapter fell back to "85 % of the lowest
     opening".
   - `blind_refs`: the case's own refs (`cost:`, `po:`, `fc:`, `sc:`, `news:`, a cheaper alternative quote) cited
     by ID with no figure of ours; the arena checks the ID against its own data. Before, the adapter cited nothing
     on an unknown supplier.
   - On all 10 hosted practice cases the data has the evidence, so **A4 plays exactly like A3 there** (checked
     offline): no risk to the practice results.
2. **`proto/final.py`, the Live Final runner** (there was none for this engine):
   - polls the waves and plays every case of a running wave in parallel, A4 through the data adapter;
   - follows the wave's cap on every poll (the host may extend a wave);
   - waits for a free session slot instead of losing the case;
   - never reads /events, /screen, /leaderboard or /results;
   - `--rehearse` for free dress rehearsals.
3. **Engine robustness**:
   - after a restart, the engine resumes our running final session instead of losing the case;
   - a crash takes the best offer that beats our alternative instead of walking away;
   - the cap is read live.
4. Tests: 4 new (wave loop, cap extension, a broken case, a full key, resume); 35 pass.

## Final-runner rehearsals (A4, cases started at once like a wave)

| Rehearsal | Plays | Result | Time left at close |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8-min cap | D01 ×2, D02 ×2 | 0.990, 0.996, 0.682, 0.682 · 4/4 deals | 338–436 s |
| 8-min cap, uncached | D01, D02 ×3 | 0.991, 0.682, 0.682, 0.703 · 4/4 deals | 270–386 s |
| **150-s cap**, uncached (stress) | D01, D02 | 0.977, 0.661 · 2/2 deals | 82 s, 53 s |

Closed after the cap: **0 of 12**.

## Caveats
- **The sandbox caches supplier replies to identical e-mails.** A deterministic engine sends the same e-mails every
  time, so repeats can be echoes (replies in 0.1 s), not new samples. Several "0.740 ×3" / "0.682 ×3" runs above
  are partly that. `--fresh` (a reference number in the subject) gives independent repeats; those are marked
  "uncached".
- 2 sandbox plays were lost to `429: at most 10 open sessions per key` while teammates also played. The runner now
  waits for a slot instead.
- Remaining gap on D02 vs the hand-written facts: 0.684 vs 0.740. The hand-written version knows the suppliers' cash
  needs and that the news "points to easing bar costs". The next sandbox ideas: cash-need cues from the supplier's
  own words, and reading the news direction.

## Decision needed: practice (costs team quota, 149 left)
- **4 weak cases** (P08, P10, P11, P18) through the final runner: 4 sessions. Pre-flight plus Tugra's planned
  retest; our board sits at 0.39–0.71 on those.
- **1 case pre-flight**: 1 session.
- **All 10 hosted cases**: 10 sessions.

### E18 · Friend's D02 replay → three ideas (running)
- **Replay:** [e843da929222686e](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/e843da929222686e) (D02, **0.661**: J1 €14.10 FCA, 14 d, 35 d). Ours: A 0.640 (3/3), A2 0.626 (mean of 3), best single search run 0.724.
- **What the friend does differently:**
  1. **Staggered RFQ opening.** Messages only C1 (cheapest quote) first. C1 answers with a €15.50 alternative. Then opens J1 *citing that fresh rival offer ID* (`offer:DEMO-C1-1-a`, verified): J1 drops **€17.10 → €14.60 / €14.50 in one step** ("which beats the Polish offer you mentioned"). We message both at once in round 0 with no rival info, and J1 reaches only €15.00–15.40 there.
  2. **Breakdown argument in the body:** "Your attached cost breakdown shows €5.56 material, €4.39 labour and €2.81 conversion, or €12.76 direct cost. A 24-month award with quick payment supports a positive margin at our proposed price." J1: "You are right about the direct costs…" → €14.60 → €14.10.
  3. **Volume framing for the supplier's motives:** "planning baseline 500 per month", "predictable 500-unit monthly orders", "a 42-day lead avoids overtime", "if a larger binding lot would change the price, quote the exact trade-off".
  4. Also: LLM-written, persona-tailored text; no push after J1's final offer.
- **Implemented as switches** (`Config.rfq_stagger`, `breakdown_arg`, `volume_framing`); variants **F** = A2 + stagger, **G** = A2 + breakdown + framing, **H** = A2 + all three.
- **Test:** D02 × 3 for F, G, H; D01 × 1 for G, H (F only changes RFQs).
- **Run 1:** F 0.746 / 0.724 / **0.374**; G 0.682 / 0.640 / 0.664 (D01 0.969); H 0.745 / **0.374** / 0.746 (D01 0.957).
- **Bug in the stagger (the two 0.374 runs):** J1 was **never contacted**. C1 (the lead) answered in < 1 s per round; J1's worker waited for "the lead's reply" but kept seeing the lead's *next* message in flight, so it waited its full 40 s while C1 negotiated 4 rounds alone and the case closed on C1 at €15.80. **Fix:** the others wait only for the lead's *first* reply; the lead pauses after round 0 until every supplier has its first message; and the engine never closes while a supplier is still untouched (`untouched` in `hold_close`).
- **Run 2 (fixed):** **F 0.740 / 0.740 / 0.703 (mean 0.728)**, H 0.745 / 0.724 / 0.703 (0.724). No outliers.
- **Verdict:** ✅ **the staggered RFQ opening is worth +0.10 on D02** (0.626 → 0.728), above the friend's 0.661, with no cost on D01 (single supplier: unchanged 0.979). **F becomes the main algorithm (A3).** Breakdown argument + volume framing (G) add +0.04 on their own but nothing on top of the stagger and −0.01 to −0.02 on D01, so they stay optional and should be tested on practice, where suppliers keep asking "which volume can you commit to?".

Checked: all modules import on the team's `arena_kit` fork; no keys, no run logs, no backups in the commit. `main` and `arda` untouched.

### E20 · Confirmation run of A3 (sandbox)
- **D01 × 2: 0.979, 0.979** — €49.50, 24 months, 30 days, from 2026-12-01 (C €409,475 vs c_best €408,624, +0.2 %).
- **D02 × 5: 0.740 in all five runs** — J1 agreed to our own sheet: **€14.12 DAP**, 14-day payment, 28-day lead (C €171,700 vs c_best €156,739).
- With the per-thread clocks, in-flight guard and staggered opening, D02 is now **deterministic** (it varied 0.535–0.724 before E14/E17/E18).
- **A3 sandbox mean: 0.860** (A2 0.803, A 0.810, naive 0.20). Sessions: D01 `b92d1fdc8ae2efef`, `ba6de0ecff39b201`; D02 `86e57a24b03f54af`, `2e11f7fc965cfad1`, `19a6cc85b7817bd5`, `ac375542dca50b34`, `8ea91bef7fea9c2e`.

### E21 · A3 on 5 practice cases → diagnosis (5 sessions, quota 149 → 144)
Table: [[Runs/2026-10-10-practice-algorithm-A3]].

| Case | A (E16) | **A3** | Teammate best | Read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P05 RFQ, 3 suppliers | 0.510 | **0.614** ✅ | 0.41 | the staggered opening helps on real suppliers too |
| P08 raw material | 0.474 | 0.350 | 0.515 | met the index clause too late (round 3), with a 12-month contract and 14-day payment |
| P10 capacity | 0.000 | **0.000** | 0.655 | new failure mode, see below |
| P11 quality | 0.378 | 0.378 | 0.71 | "say fixed" fired, but the price stalled at €47.50 (800 ppm / €300 chargeback) |
| P18 raw material | 0.286 | 0.282 | 0.386 | same as P08 |

**Why (from our logs and the teammate's best runs in `Team-Knowledge/Runs/`):**
1. **P10:** the bottleneck anchor was based on *total cost*, but the supplier's opening covers only 12 months, so its C is inflated by a half-year of uncovered need at the fallback price + 25 % risk. "3 % below the opening C" became one **12-month, 56-day package at €31.65**. The supplier then **cut the volume to 19,890** (below the must-have 22,230: the case is literally "Ravensteiner cuts the seal allocation"). In round 2 the guards left no valid package, and the engine **walked away with no alternative** → 0. The teammate's 0.655: first message **24 months, full 23,400 volume, 56-day lead**, ~10 % below the opening *price* → accepted at €31.80.
2. **P11:** the teammate's deal is **300 ppm with zero chargeback** at €45.50 ("we can do the 300 ppm with zero chargebacks"). Suppliers price penalty clauses far higher than their expected cost; we kept getting 800 ppm / €300 chargeback at €47.50.
3. **P08 / P18:** both suppliers declared the AS-14404 clause *mandatory* in their **first** reply. Our meet-fields waited for two insistences (round 3, after they went final), and the met package kept the wrong levers (12-month contract, 14-day payment). The teammate took the **clause in round 1 with 90-day payment** (P08 C €1,045k vs our €1,074k; P18 €267k vs €275k).

**Fixes → A4:** (a) bottleneck anchor on **price** (≥ opening price × 0.97) with full need volume and a contract ≥ horizon; (b) **never walk without an alternative**: if no package survives the guards, counter at their price with the must-haves restored; (c) **meet a term at its first explicit insistence** ("mandatory", "essential", "requires", "not possible") by changing only that field in our best package; (d) rank packages with the supplier's dislike of **chargebacks** (penalty aversion ×3) so "strict ppm, no chargeback" is offered; (e) suppliers with good credit get a low cash rate (0.05), so long payment terms rank first.

### E22 · Algorithm A4 (fixes from E21) on the 4 weak practice cases (4 sessions, quota 144 → 140)
- **Code (A4 = A3 +):** bottleneck anchor on **price** (opening price × 0.90, as the teammate's P10 run) with full coverage; packages above the supplier's price are **capped at its price** instead of dropped; **full-coverage packages first**; **never walk without an alternative** (fallback counter at its price with the must-haves restored); **meet a term at its first explicit insistence** ("mandatory", "essential", …) by changing only that field in our best package; **penalty aversion ×3** when ranking packages (chargebacks); good-credit suppliers get cash rate 0.05 (long payment ranks first).
- **Sandbox regression:** D01 0.979, D02 0.740 ×3: unchanged ✅.
- **Practice:** **P10 0.000 → 0.679** (new case record, teammate 0.655) · **P11 0.378 → 0.710** (= record) · P08 0.350 → 0.482 (teammate 0.515) · P18 0.282 → **0.245** ❌ (teammate 0.386). Table: [[Runs/2026-10-10-practice-algorithm-A4]].
- **P18 trace:** the clause package was met in round 2 at **€5.37** (too aggressive: "we cannot offer further price reductions"), then **dropped again in round 3**. The supplier went final with *worse* terms (36 months, 60 days) and we took €5.80. Next (sandbox-only until approved): keep a met term in a package for all later rounds, and price the met package nearer to the supplier's offer.
- **Process rule from now on:** every practice run needs the user's explicit OK (quota is shared by the team). This run was already in progress when the rule was given.

### E23 · Generalisation audit, generic P18 fix, stalled-reply fix (all free: sandbox + offline)
**Question (Tugra):** are the fixes hard-coded? The final has cases and suppliers we have never seen.

**Audit of the code** (searched `proto/` for case IDs, supplier IDs, part numbers, index names, magic prices):

| Part | Hard-coded? | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Tactics (curve, rounds, 2 packages, pushes, holds, staggered RFQ, guards) | no | generic rules; their *parameters* were tuned on D01/D02 and checked on 10 practice cases |
| A2/A4/A5 fixes | no | each triggers on a **case feature** (goal type, must-haves, no alternative, a term the supplier introduced or insisted on, chargeback fields), never on an ID |
| Practice/final adapter | no | facts and floors from `facts.json` / SQL for whatever case arrives |
| `FACTS`, `CASH_RATE`, foundry sentence in `engine.py` | ⚠️ **yes** | sandbox-only, now marked as such and **no longer used by default** (`variants.py --handfacts` to reproduce old runs) |

**Changes:**
1. **One generic code path for everything** (the final's): case reference IDs the data does not know are cited by type without inventing figures; floors from the supplier's own cost breakdown / material share (arena document formats) before should-cost.
2. **Generic P18 fix (A5):** a term the supplier insisted on stays in one of our packages for every later round (`t.met`), priced at most 3 % below its own price (`meet_band=0.03`).
3. **Stalled replies under load:** slow sessions waited exactly 180 s (the kit's HTTP timeout) and then got the stored answer by retry, by which time the supplier's 60-second clock had run out three times → "session has ended: timeout" (even in single-supplier D01). **Fix:** `ArenaClient(timeout=25, retries=7)` re-fetches a stalled answer every 25 s (safe: same move ID, the arena never acts twice). Also: a close on an already-ended session now reads the arena's result instead of crashing.

**Results:**
- **Generic code only, sandbox:** **A5 D01 0.982, D02 0.703 ×3 (mean 0.843)**, vs 0.979 / 0.740 (0.860) with the hand-written sandbox facts. The hand-written facts were worth ~0.04 on D02 (mostly one sentence about market news that generic code correctly does not invent). **0.843 is the honest sandbox number** for what the final would run.
- **Unseen case types (offline smoke, all 19 practice case files, incl. the 9 never played: P06 RFQ/stabilise, P09 capacity, P12 quality, P13 price increase/leverage, P14 renewal/no alternative, P15 bundling, P16 steel index, P17 component costs, P19 renewal):** no crash, every package within the must-haves, 2 packages and 1–6 data-backed facts each.
- **Not yet tested on practice:** the P18 fix (needs quota; ask first).
- **Remaining overfitting risk:** the tactic *parameters* (e=2, T=4, anchor −3 %, 2 packages, pushes) come from 3 demo suppliers + 10 practice cases. The rules are generic; their tuning is not fully proven on unseen suppliers.

### E24 · Confirmation run of A5 (generic code path, sandbox)
- **D01 × 2: 0.982, 0.982**: €49.50, 24 months, 30 days, from 2027-01-01 (C €409,339 vs c_best €408,624, +0.2 %).
- **D02 × 5: 0.703, 0.703, 0.703, 0.718, 0.701 (mean 0.706)**: J1 €13.83–13.91 FCA, 14-day payment, 28-day lead (C ≈ €173–174k vs c_best €156.7k). No timeouts, no errors.
- **Sandbox mean 0.844** with generic code only (A3 with hand-written facts: 0.860).

1. **P10:** the bottleneck anchor was based on *total cost*, but the supplier's opening covers only 12 months, so its C is inflated by a half-year of uncovered need at the fallback price + 25 % risk. "3 % below the opening C" became one **12-month, 56-day package at €31.65**. The supplier then **cut the volume to 19,890** (below the must-have 22,230: the case is literally "Ravensteiner cuts the seal allocation"). In round 2 the guards left no valid package, and the engine **walked away with no alternative** → 0. The teammate's 0.655: first message **24 months, full 23,400 volume, 56-day lead**, ~10 % below the opening *price* → accepted at €31.80.
2. **P11:** the teammate's deal is **300 ppm with zero chargeback** at €45.50 ("we can do the 300 ppm with zero chargebacks"). Suppliers price penalty clauses far higher than their expected cost; we kept getting 800 ppm / €300 chargeback at €47.50.
3. **P08 / P18:** both suppliers declared the AS-14404 clause *mandatory* in their **first** reply. Our meet-fields waited for two insistences (round 3, after they went final), and the met package kept the wrong levers (12-month contract, 14-day payment). The teammate took the **clause in round 1 with 90-day payment** (P08 C €1,045k vs our €1,074k; P18 €267k vs €275k).

**Fixes → A4:** (a) bottleneck anchor on **price** (≥ opening price × 0.97) with full need volume and a contract ≥ horizon; (b) **never walk without an alternative**: if no package survives the guards, counter at their price with the must-haves restored; (c) **meet a term at its first explicit insistence** ("mandatory", "essential", "requires", "not possible") by changing only that field in our best package; (d) rank packages with the supplier's dislike of **chargebacks** (penalty aversion ×3) so "strict ppm, no chargeback" is offered; (e) suppliers with good credit get a low cash rate (0.05), so long payment terms rank first.

### E22 · Algorithm A4 (fixes from E21) on the 4 weak practice cases (4 sessions, quota 144 → 140)
- **Code (A4 = A3 +):** bottleneck anchor on **price** (opening price × 0.90, as the teammate's P10 run) with full coverage; packages above the supplier's price are **capped at its price** instead of dropped; **full-coverage packages first**; **never walk without an alternative** (fallback counter at its price with the must-haves restored); **meet a term at its first explicit insistence** ("mandatory", "essential", …) by changing only that field in our best package; **penalty aversion ×3** when ranking packages (chargebacks); good-credit suppliers get cash rate 0.05 (long payment ranks first).
- **Sandbox regression:** D01 0.979, D02 0.740 ×3: unchanged ✅.
- **Practice:** **P10 0.000 → 0.679** (new case record, teammate 0.655) · **P11 0.378 → 0.710** (= record) · P08 0.350 → 0.482 (teammate 0.515) · P18 0.282 → **0.245** ❌ (teammate 0.386). Table: [[Runs/2026-10-10-practice-algorithm-A4]].
- **P18 trace:** the clause package was met in round 2 at **€5.37** (too aggressive: "we cannot offer further price reductions"), then **dropped again in round 3**. The supplier went final with *worse* terms (36 months, 60 days) and we took €5.80. Next (sandbox-only until approved): keep a met term in a package for all later rounds, and price the met package nearer to the supplier's offer.
- **Process rule from now on:** every practice run needs the user's explicit OK (quota is shared by the team). This run was already in progress when the rule was given.

### E23 · Generalisation audit, generic P18 fix, stalled-reply fix (all free: sandbox + offline)
**Question (Tugra):** are the fixes hard-coded? The final has cases and suppliers we have never seen.

**Audit of the code** (searched `proto/` for case IDs, supplier IDs, part numbers, index names, magic prices):

| Part | Hard-coded? | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Tactics (curve, rounds, 2 packages, pushes, holds, staggered RFQ, guards) | no | generic rules; their *parameters* were tuned on D01/D02 and checked on 10 practice cases |
| A2/A4/A5 fixes | no | each triggers on a **case feature** (goal type, must-haves, no alternative, a term the supplier introduced or insisted on, chargeback fields), never on an ID |
| Practice/final adapter | no | facts and floors from `facts.json` / SQL for whatever case arrives |
| `FACTS`, `CASH_RATE`, foundry sentence in `engine.py` | ⚠️ **yes** | sandbox-only, now marked as such and **no longer used by default** (`variants.py --handfacts` to reproduce old runs) |

**Changes:**
1. **One generic code path for everything** (the final's): case reference IDs the data does not know are cited by type without inventing figures; floors from the supplier's own cost breakdown / material share (arena document formats) before should-cost.
2. **Generic P18 fix (A5):** a term the supplier insisted on stays in one of our packages for every later round (`t.met`), priced at most 3 % below its own price (`meet_band=0.03`).
3. **Stalled replies under load:** slow sessions waited exactly 180 s (the kit's HTTP timeout) and then got the stored answer by retry, by which time the supplier's 60-second clock had run out three times → "session has ended: timeout" (even in single-supplier D01). **Fix:** `ArenaClient(timeout=25, retries=7)` re-fetches a stalled answer every 25 s (safe: same move ID, the arena never acts twice). Also: a close on an already-ended session now reads the arena's result instead of crashing.

**Results:**
- **Generic code only, sandbox:** **A5 D01 0.982, D02 0.703 ×3 (mean 0.843)**, vs 0.979 / 0.740 (0.860) with the hand-written sandbox facts. The hand-written facts were worth ~0.04 on D02 (mostly one sentence about market news that generic code correctly does not invent). **0.843 is the honest sandbox number** for what the final would run.
- **Unseen case types (offline smoke, all 19 practice case files, incl. the 9 never played: P06 RFQ/stabilise, P09 capacity, P12 quality, P13 price increase/leverage, P14 renewal/no alternative, P15 bundling, P16 steel index, P17 component costs, P19 renewal):** no crash, every package within the must-haves, 2 packages and 1–6 data-backed facts each.
- **Not yet tested on practice:** the P18 fix (needs quota; ask first).
- **Remaining overfitting risk:** the tactic *parameters* (e=2, T=4, anchor −3 %, 2 packages, pushes) come from 3 demo suppliers + 10 practice cases. The rules are generic; their tuning is not fully proven on unseen suppliers.

### E24 · Confirmation run of A5 (generic code path, sandbox)
- **D01 × 2: 0.982, 0.982**: €49.50, 24 months, 30 days, from 2027-01-01 (C €409,339 vs c_best €408,624, +0.2 %).
- **D02 × 5: 0.703, 0.703, 0.703, 0.718, 0.701 (mean 0.706)**: J1 €13.83–13.91 FCA, 14-day payment, 28-day lead (C ≈ €173–174k vs c_best €156.7k). No timeouts, no errors.
- **Sandbox mean 0.844** with generic code only (A3 with hand-written facts: 0.860).

- **Mean 0.614** (teammate's best-per-case 0.602). **New records: P03 0.923, P01 0.881** (own best). **P05 = 0** (critical RFQ bug). Best per case over all our runs: **0.703**.
- Every result, every problem with evidence and the fix plan: [[Practice-Run-A5-Findings]].

# Practice run A5 (all 10 hosted cases): every result and every problem

Algorithm A5 on the generic code path (what the final runs). 10 practice sessions (quota 140 → 130), 2026-10-10 evening, arena under heavy load (supplier replies up to ~113 s). Raw table with replays: [[Runs/2026-10-10-practice-algorithm-A5]]. Full transcripts: `starter-kit/proto/runs/variants/A5/` (extract with `proto/inspect_run.py A5`).

## Results

| Case | Type · goal | **A5** | Best before | Teammate | Record | Deal | C_deal vs C_best | Rounds / s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | price increase · stabilise | **0.881** ⭐ | 0.801 | 0.76 | 0.928 | €133.10, 30 d, from 2027-01-01 (supplier *agreed* to our 2nd sheet) | 1,103,602 vs 1,096,816 (+0.6 %) | 3 / 135 |
| P02 | price increase · stabilise | 0.679 | 0.684 | 0.18 | 0.684 | €360.32, 60 d, CU clause (deadband 5 %): *agreed* to our 2nd sheet | 2,250,731 vs 2,235,514 (+0.7 %) | 2 / 62 |
| P03 | renewal · stabilise | **0.923** ⭐ new record | 0.866 | 0.83 | 0.903 | €432.15, 90 d, 24 mo | 3,935,069 vs 3,909,043 (+0.7 %) | 3 / 79 |
| P04 | renewal · routine | 0.810 | 0.874 | 0.86 | 0.874 | €4.91, 60 d, 36 mo (final at round 3) | 196,970 vs 196,529 (+0.2 %) | 3 / 68 |
| **P05** | RFQ, 3 suppliers · leverage | **0.000** ❌ | 0.614 | 0.41 | 0.676 | **no deal**: two suppliers *agreed*, both lost (bug 1) | – | 4 / 214 |
| P07 | bundling · routine | 0.710 | 0.699 | 0.70 | 0.779 | €5.43, 60 d, 36 mo (final) | 325,829 vs 299,241 (+8.9 %) | 5 / 102 |
| P08 | raw material · leverage | 0.482 | 0.482 | 0.515 | 0.593 | €5.44, 14 d, 36 mo, AS-14404 clause (5 %) | 1,051,250 vs 960,309 (+9.5 %) | 4 / 67 |
| P10 | capacity · secure supply | 0.679 | 0.679 | 0.655 | 0.679 | €31.50, 36 mo, 23,400/yr, 56-day lead (final) | 1,522,963 vs 1,328,927 (+14.6 %) | 2 / 30 |
| P11 | quality · quality first | 0.710 | 0.710 | 0.71 | 0.71 | €45.50, 300 ppm, no chargeback (final) | 750,083 vs 722,500 (+3.8 %) | 4 / 7 |
| P18 | raw material · leverage | 0.270 | 0.286 | 0.386 | 0.43 | €5.80, 90 d, 24 mo, AS-14404 clause (5 %) | 275,561 vs 222,651 (+23.8 %) | 3 / 86 |
| **Mean** | | **0.614** | | 0.602 | | | | |

**Best per case over all our runs: 0.703** (P01 0.881, P02 0.684, P03 0.923, P04 0.874, P05 0.614, P07 0.710, P08 0.482, P10 0.679, P11 0.710, P18 0.286).

## Problems, most severe first

### 1. ❌ Critical: an agreed RFQ deal was lost while we waited (P05 = 0)
- **Evidence:** Dralveck (70210) **agreed** to our sheet at €29.27 (received at 161 s); Fuchsreiter (70250) agreed at €29.97 (193 s). The closing guard waited because a rival reply was in flight. We sent the accept at 207 s, and the arena answered: *"late: more than 60 s after the supplier's last move, so it counted as a timeout (your last offer, repeated)"*. The agreed sheet was no longer standing (`422 not a standing offer`). Our fallback then treated the session as ended and stopped, so **no deal**.
- **Why:** (a) under load the supplier's move happened well before we *received* it (replies took 48–113 s to arrive), so our "45 s of waiting" was really > 60 s on the arena's clock; (b) after a failed accept we gave up instead of re-reading the thread and accepting the new standing sheet.
- **Fix:** accept an `agreed` (or acceptable final) offer **at once**, never hold it for a rival; on a late/422 accept, **GET the thread and accept its current standing sheet**; never end our side of a live session after a failed close.

### 2. ❌ High: packages that were not equal in cost to us (P02)
- **Evidence:** round 2 sent €364.50 / 90 d (C 2,235,459 ≈ C_best) and €360.32 / 60 d + CU clause (C 2,256,842). The supplier agreed to the **clause package, €21k worse for us**.
- **Why:** "equal C" tolerance was 1 % of C (€22k), larger than the whole room of this case (2.1 % open → best).
- **Fix:** tolerance = min(0.2 % of C, 10 % of the room open → target).

### 3. ❌ High: an insisted term was dropped again (P18)
- **Evidence:** round 1 the supplier made the AS-14404 clause a condition; we met it (€5.53, clause, 90 d). Round 3 our packages had **no clause** again; the supplier hardened and went final at €5.70–5.80.
- **Why (bug):** the "never in our sheets" check rejected the term in round 3 *because we had offered it in round 2*.
- **Fix:** a term we have met stays met (skip that check for persisted terms).

### 4. ⚠️ Medium: we let a better earlier offer go (P18, P08)
- **Evidence:** P18 round 1 alternative €5.70 + clause (5 %) / 60 d had C 272,612; after our push the final offers were C 275,561–278,691. P08: round 3 we switched to 14-day payment / 36 months and ended at C 1,051,250 vs 1,050,224 standing a round earlier.
- **Fix:** track the best offer seen; when a supplier's offers get worse after our move and it is close to final, stop pushing and accept the best standing one.

### 5. ⚠️ Medium: requests for proof we never answered (P03, P04, P05, P08, P11)
- **Evidence:** *"Which figures is that based on? Please send us the data."* (P03, P08, P11), *"Please provide proof of this total requirement so we can verify it"* (P04), *"we would need some proof for these figures"* (P05).
- **Fix:** when a supplier asks for data or proof, **attach a short data sheet** with the facts we cited (IDs and the values from `facts.json`: forecast change, order prices, scorecard, should-cost).

### 6. ⚠️ Medium: our target is too timid where the room is big (P07, P08, P18, P10)
- **Evidence:** P07 target C 318,889 vs C_best 299,241 (our first ask was already 6 % above the best possible); P08 975,580 vs 960,309; P18 256,608 vs 222,651; P10 1,260,946 vs 1,328,927 (here too bold).
- **Why:** without a supplier breakdown or should-cost, the floor is "current price / (1 + margin) × drift", capped at the opening, which says little about real room.
- **Fix (to test):** use the supplier's stated material share ("Material accounts for about 61 %") and the material index move to bound the floor; keep the bottleneck rule for `secure_supply`.

### 7. ⚠️ Medium: "price frozen, talk about terms" was not used (P03)
- **Evidence:** *"Our management has frozen all price reductions until December 2027. We can talk about the terms instead – payment, volume or contract length."* We kept asking for price.
- **Fix (to test):** when a supplier freezes price, offer packages that change only terms (contract length, payment, volume) at its price.

### 8. Info: arena load
- Supplier replies took 1–113 s (P05). The 25-second re-fetch fix (E23) kept every other case inside its clocks, but P05 shows how tight the 60-second window gets in RFQs under load.

## Fix plan → A6
1. Accept agreed/final offers immediately; recover from late/422 accepts (problem 1).
2. Tight equal-C tolerance relative to the room (problem 2).
3. Persist met terms (problem 3).
4. Best-seen guard near the end (problem 4).
5. Proof/data attachment on request (problem 5).
6. Tested on the sandbox (free) and the offline smoke test of all 19 case files first; practice only after the team's OK.

### 3. ❌ High: an insisted term was dropped again (P18)
- **Evidence:** round 1 the supplier made the AS-14404 clause a condition; we met it (€5.53, clause, 90 d). Round 3 our packages had **no clause** again; the supplier hardened and went final at €5.70–5.80.
- **Why (bug):** the "never in our sheets" check rejected the term in round 3 *because we had offered it in round 2*.
- **Fix:** a term we have met stays met (skip that check for persisted terms).

### 4. ⚠️ Medium: we let a better earlier offer go (P18, P08)
- **Evidence:** P18 round 1 alternative €5.70 + clause (5 %) / 60 d had C 272,612; after our push the final offers were C 275,561–278,691. P08: round 3 we switched to 14-day payment / 36 months and ended at C 1,051,250 vs 1,050,224 standing a round earlier.
- **Fix:** track the best offer seen; when a supplier's offers get worse after our move and it is close to final, stop pushing and accept the best standing one.

### 5. ⚠️ Medium: requests for proof we never answered (P03, P04, P05, P08, P11)
- **Evidence:** *"Which figures is that based on? Please send us the data."* (P03, P08, P11), *"Please provide proof of this total requirement so we can verify it"* (P04), *"we would need some proof for these figures"* (P05).
- **Fix:** when a supplier asks for data or proof, **attach a short data sheet** with the facts we cited (IDs and the values from `facts.json`: forecast change, order prices, scorecard, should-cost).

### 6. ⚠️ Medium: our target is too timid where the room is big (P07, P08, P18, P10)
- **Evidence:** P07 target C 318,889 vs C_best 299,241 (our first ask was already 6 % above the best possible); P08 975,580 vs 960,309; P18 256,608 vs 222,651; P10 1,260,946 vs 1,328,927 (here too bold).
- **Why:** without a supplier breakdown or should-cost, the floor is "current price / (1 + margin) × drift", capped at the opening, which says little about real room.
- **Fix (to test):** use the supplier's stated material share ("Material accounts for about 61 %") and the material index move to bound the floor; keep the bottleneck rule for `secure_supply`.

### 7. ⚠️ Medium: "price frozen, talk about terms" was not used (P03)
- **Evidence:** *"Our management has frozen all price reductions until December 2027. We can talk about the terms instead – payment, volume or contract length."* We kept asking for price.
- **Fix (to test):** when a supplier freezes price, offer packages that change only terms (contract length, payment, volume) at its price.

### 8. Info: arena load
- Supplier replies took 1–113 s (P05). The 25-second re-fetch fix (E23) kept every other case inside its clocks, but P05 shows how tight the 60-second window gets in RFQs under load.

## Fix plan → A6
1. Accept agreed/final offers immediately; recover from late/422 accepts (problem 1).
2. Tight equal-C tolerance relative to the room (problem 2).
3. Persist met terms (problem 3).
4. Best-seen guard near the end (problem 4).
5. Proof/data attachment on request (problem 5).
6. Tested on the sandbox (free) and the offline smoke test of all 19 case files first; practice only after the team's OK.

# Exact D02 algorithm that reproducibly scored 0.661

Implementation: `EvidenceTraderAgent(d02_style="j1_cost", d02_target_cost=170638.57)` in
`starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/evidence.py`, ehl-tacto commit `4bf381e` on branch
`sudeep/negotiation-experiments`. The batch configuration is
`starter-kit/experiments/qualification.json`. This is a **deterministic, demo-specific state
machine**. It uses fixed bid templates and evidence IDs; there is no LLM, reinforcement learning,
or fitted opponent model in this policy.

## Inputs and invariant checks

- Read the D02 case plus both current supplier threads, including quote attachments and any
  alternative term sheets in the latest supplier reply.
- For each current supplier sheet, fill missing fields from that supplier's quote PDF/standard
  terms. Reject sheets whose resulting lead time exceeds **42 days**. This rejects C1's opening
  €16.00 quote because its omitted lead time defaults to **45 days**.
- Calculate **complete buyer cost** over 6,000 units/year for 24 months: purchases + payment
  financing + freight + lateness beyond 35 days + expected quality loss. Choose by this cost, not
  the lowest unit price. Only a current, valid supplier sheet can be accepted.
- If any valid standing sheet has cost **≤ €170,638.57**, accept the cheapest such sheet immediately.
  This threshold corresponds to the D02 score needed for the team's combined 0.8 gate given the
  repeated D01 score. No D02 sheet reached it in the recorded runs.

## Message state machine

Each supplier's state is the number of buyer emails already sent to that thread. All bid sheets
use **14-day payment**; the case fixes the contract at **24 months**. The email states the real
**6,000-unit annual requirement**; the agent never invents a larger commitment.

| Decision point | Supplier and exact structured bids (`€/unit`, Incoterm, lead days) | Evidence and purpose |
|---|---|---|
| C1 has 0 buyer emails | C1: `14.50 EXW 42`, `14.80 FCA 42`, `15.00 DAP 35` | Cite `fc:SH-220@2026-09`; get a valid competing quote while offering 14-day cash and flexible delivery. C1 replied with a valid **€15.50 EXW / 42-day** alternative. |
| J1 has 0 buyer emails | J1: `13.80 DAP 35`, `13.40 EXW 42`, `14.00 FCA 35` | Name C1's **actual current valid** price, terms and offer ID; cite `news:N-0412`. J1 verified the rival quote and news claims, then countered **€14.60 FCA / 35 days**. |
| J1 has 1 buyer email | J1: `13.40 EXW 42`, `13.80 DAP 35`, `13.60 FCA 35` | Cite `cost:part:SH-220` and `sc:DEMO-J1@2026Q3`. Mention J1's €5.56 material + €4.39 labour + €2.81 conversion breakdown **only if those figures appear in its attachment**. J1 verified both references and countered **€14.10 FCA / 35 days**, plus €13.90 EXW / 42 days. |
| C1 has 1 buyer email | C1: `15.25 EXW 42`, `15.50 FCA 35` | Cite `cost:part:SH-220` and `sc:DEMO-C1@2026Q3`; ask for a price on the same 6,000-unit volume. Its later offer was €15.30 EXW / 42 days. |
| Later C1 email | C1: `max(13.50, latest main price − 0.25)` EXW/42; second FCA/35 bid is €0.25 higher | No new references; compare its reply with J1's standing offer. |
| Later J1 email | J1: `13.60 EXW 42`, `14.00 DAP 35`, `13.80 FCA 35` | No new references. J1 marked **€14.10 FCA / 35 days final**. The email did not repeat the direct-cost figures; J1 nevertheless referred back to its overhead in its response. |

Supplier choice is exact: contact C1 first, then J1; give J1 its first follow-up before returning
to C1. After that, choose the active supplier with fewer buyer emails, breaking ties toward C1.
`agreed` and `final_offer` threads remain available for acceptance but receive no further bids.
When no productive thread remains, or the selected thread has four buyer emails, accept the
**cheapest current feasible offer**. In the recorded run this was J1's `offer:DEMO-J1-3`. Its
€14.10 FCA/35-day package cost less overall than J1's €13.90 EXW/42-day alternative because EXW
added freight and seven days of lateness.

## Verified reproduction

The same committed policy ran in **three fresh D02 sandbox sessions** in the qualification batch.
Each ended with `sup:DEMO-J1`, `offer:DEMO-J1-3`: **€14.10/unit, 14-day payment, 35-day lead, FCA**.
Every run had total buyer cost **€176,257.60**, official score **0.6608797297715212**, and a deal.
The replays are [run 1](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/e843da929222686e),
[run 2](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/a40f20f453858602), and
[run 3](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/e38acad546436805). The score follows the arena formula:

To run the same policy again from `ehl-tacto/starter-kit`, with the team API key in the ignored
`.env` and `ARENA_URL` pointing at the hosted arena:

```bash

```
