action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

**One fix joins the final build.** Re-reading all 284 arena records, I found a live bug in the frozen build. I sent MAIN my findings and it received them. It's now checking my first proposed rule (bolder first asks) against a deeper-first-ask pass it already ran tonight. It has sent a reply, which should arrive here when this turn ends, and I'll pass it on.

**What MAIN had decided before my message:**
- The fact planner plus the RFQ rival loop scored 0.715, no gain. The final build stays A9h, plus one fix: it now cites only data IDs in `facts.json`. An unchecked P05 forecast ID had drawn a "contradicted" verdict.
- It recommends no more engine changes tonight: it sees no credible path to 0.8, and every change risks the unseen cases. 244 practice sessions are left for Sunday's pre-flight check.
- It left one lead on purpose. On P02 our cost model slightly underrates the supplier's cost of money, which costs about 0.08. MAIN judged the fix too risky the night before the final.

**What I sent:**
- **The run:** the 0.715 run equals the previous build. The planner ran out of facts, and suppliers still went final by round 3–4.
- **Where the points went:**
  - On P05, P07 and P18 our first ask was already at or above the price that would reach the record, so no later move could get there.
  - On P08 we raised our ask while the supplier barely moved.
  - On P02 we accepted the copper-clause package, and the clause plus the relationship charge cost €50k.
- **What moves these suppliers** (1,114 replies from our stored sessions): when we move our price and a fact lands, they concede 82 % of the time; when we hold with no fact, 27 %. Citing our own order prices landed 0 of 198 times.
- **Three proposed rules:**
  1. Bolder first asks in leverage and routine cases.
  2. Concede only when the supplier moves.
  3. Accept by total cost, including clause risk and the relationship charge.
- **Pointers:** file locations, and the pieces of my R4 fork worth porting.

**Where we stand:** we agree more facts won't help. Where we differ is whether a price-path rule is worth one more test before the freeze. If MAIN's anchor pass already rules out (1), then (2) and (3) are the only candidates left.

Nothing has been built or committed, and no practice sessions were used.

# ehl-tacto

Team of 4 at the EHL Grand Finale (Munich, 10-11 Oct 2026), Tacto track: an AI buyer agent that negotiates
by e-mail with hosted supplier bots on https://arena.tacto.ai. Forked from
[tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit) (`upstream` remote).

**Live Final: Sun 11 Oct 12:00, code freeze at the same moment.** No human in the loop; the agent must
not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results` during the final.

## Shared knowledge: `vault/` (RxV00's Obsidian vault; our notes live in `vault/Team-Knowledge/`)
Start every task by reading `vault/Team-Knowledge/Home.md` and `vault/Team-Knowledge/Plan/Board.md`. Write what you learn back:
- learnings that transfer to new suppliers → `vault/Playbook/` (`agent: true` notes go into the buyer agent's prompt - keep them short)
- observations about one supplier → its note in `vault/Suppliers/`, under `## Team notes`
- what a practice run showed → the `## Team notes` of its note in `vault/Runs/`
- decisions → `vault/Decisions/` (template in `vault/Templates/`)
- move your Board card when you start or finish a task
Generated notes (`Suppliers/`, `Cases/`, `Runs/`) are rewritten by `uv run arena vault …`; only `## Team notes` sections survive.
`vault/Source/` symlinks the raw data and the brief - read, never edit.

## Layout
- `brief/` the challenge: `brief.md` (rules, score), `api.md` (API, cost formula), `submission.md`
- `data/` data package v1 (CSV, `world.sqlite`, `facts.json`, contracts, correspondence)
- `starter-kit/` Python package `arena_kit` (uv, Python 3.12): client, `play.py` runner, `cost.py` (C), `agents/llm.py`, `vault.py`
- `vault/` the Obsidian vault

## Commands (from `starter-kit/`)
```bash
uv sync --all-extras
uv run arena me                                   # key works? practice quota

# free - use these for development
uv run arena play case:D01 --agent orchestra -v         # hosted sandbox: real-style suppliers, no quota
uv run arena run --set sandbox --agent orchestra        # both sandbox cases (D01 price increase, D02 RFQ)
uv run arena run --set sandbox --agent hybrid           # Tugra's engine (proto/, A9h = A9 with A6's RFQ play) for every case, orchestra as fallback
ENGINE_VARIANT=A8 uv run arena run --set sandbox --agent hybrid   # another algorithm from proto/variants.py
ENGINE_WRITER=template uv run arena run --set sandbox --agent hybrid   # no LLM: the engine's template e-mails (default: LLM_MODEL rewrites them, template on any failure)
ENGINE_WRITER=vary uv run arena run --set sandbox --agent hybrid       # templates with a tagged subject: fresh replies on a cached arena
../scripts/sim.sh play case:P05 --agent orchestra -v    # local arena-sim, any case P01-P19/D01/D02, scripted supplier
../scripts/sim.sh run --set practice --parallel 10   # every case locally (plumbing, timing)
../scripts/sim.sh stop

# costs practice sessions (200/24 h for the whole team) - needs --practice
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent orchestra -v --practice
uv run arena run --set practice --agent orchestra --parallel 8 --practice

# the Live Final (start before 12:00, leave it running): the hybrid = Tugra's A9 with the orchestra as fallback
uv run arena run --set final --agent hybrid --parallel 10 -v > ../logs/final.log 2>&1

uv run arena dashboard                            # live view of every play/run: http://127.0.0.1:8765 (logs/events.jsonl)
uv run arena vault suppliers|cases|runs           # regenerate vault notes
uv run arena cases --save cases                   # refresh the saved case files arena-sim loads
uv run arena data                                 # data package (+ Sunday release from Sun 08:00)
uv run pytest && uv run ruff check .
```
The sandbox has 3 demo suppliers, not the practice ones. arena-sim's supplier is a plain script (opens +10 %,
concedes 2 % per term sheet): good for plumbing and timing, says nothing about real supplier behaviour.

## Rules
- Secrets only in the root `.env` (git-ignored): `CLAUDE_API_KEY` (aliased to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), `ARENA_API_KEY`. Never commit or print them.
- Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team. Ask before running a whole practice set.
- Numbers come from code, the model writes. Never cite a data ID that is not in `facts.json`.
- 60 s per message per thread; the 8-minute wave cap in the final. Keep LLM calls fast.

- [Tacto EHL challenge](tacto-ehl-challenge.md) — team of 4, negotiation agent for arena.tacto.ai, Live Final Sun 2026-10-11 12:00
- [Shared checkout commits](shared-checkout-commits.md) — other sessions switch branches and leave hunks in my files; check branch + index, commit only my hunks via a temp index
- [Sandbox first, ask before practice](sandbox-first-practice-ask.md) — test changes on sandbox D01/D02 freely; ask the user before any hosted practice run
- [Tugra base model](tugra-base-model.md) — base agent = Tugra's engine (starter-kit/proto/); A9 merged into arda, `--agent hybrid` runs it for every case; a second uncommitted fork (R4) sits in the worktree .claude/worktrees/tugra

# Options beyond tuning: how to close the gap to 0.84

Written ~21:00 on 2026-10-10 from:
- the practice board and the build page (per-case records);
- **all 284 practice sessions the team has stored** (`logs/practice_states.json`: 1,114 supplier replies with their
  back offices);
- Tugra's vault up to A12.

## Where we are

| | Mean | Note |
|---|---|---|
| NoIdea (#1) | **0.839** | holds 7 of 10 case records, with only 187 practice sessions |
| #2–#4 (gLarPC, Codacabana, TTMAR) | 0.775–0.777 | |
| **us (#7)** | **0.746** | best run per case over 284 sessions; a single full run scores 0.57–0.69 (A9 0.688, A10 0.567 with two zeros) |

The gap is concentrated in a few cases:

| Case | Record (holder) | Ours | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| P08 raw material | 0.916 (NoIdea) | 0.657 | −0.26 |
| P05 RFQ, 3 suppliers | 0.924 (TTMAR) | 0.736 | −0.19 |
| P02 copper, stabilise | 0.847 (NoIdea) | 0.684 | −0.16 |
| P18 raw material | 0.677 (NoIdea) | 0.532 | −0.15 |
| P07 bundle / P11 quality | 0.81 | 0.71 | −0.10 |
| P01, P03, P04, P10 | | | ≤ 0.04 |

**It is not more runs.** TTMAR (312 sessions), gLarPC (276) and we (284) all ran more than NoIdea (187) and score
lower. **The final is one attempt per case on unseen suppliers:** a single zero costs 10 points of a wave, so a
robust floor matters as much as a high peak.

## What the data says moves these suppliers (1,114 replies, our own sessions)

**1. A new fact that lands is the currency; our own price moves barely matter.** Rounds 2 and later:

| Our message | Supplier conceded | Mean concession | Answered with a final offer |
|---|---|---|---|
| held our price, no fact landed | 27 % | 0.40 % | 32 % |
| moved, no fact landed | 54 % | 0.93 % | 27 % |
| **moved + a fact landed** | **82 %** | **1.78 %** | **8 %** |

**2. Concessions happen in rounds 1–2.** The median concession is 1.35 % in round 1 and 1.03 % in round 2, then 0
from round 3, where 40 % of replies are final. Suppliers go final when we run out of new facts, not when we run out
of rounds.

**3. Fact types are wildly different** (how often the supplier said "it holds and we took it into account" vs "it
does not change our calculation"):

| Data we cite | Landed | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| our own past order prices | **0 of 198** | pure waste; our engines cite them constantly |
| delivery record (scorecard) | 31 % | |
| rival quote / offer | 48 % | in RFQs: 2.1 % mean concession when cited vs 0.3 % without (final 25 % vs 62 %) |
| should-cost | 76 % | |
| volume change (forecast) | 76 % | |
| index change | 84 % | we sent **79 duplicates**, spent slots |
| notice period (letter vs contract) | 96 % | |
| quality record | 100 % | |

Also from Tugra's A9: orders at *another* supplier come back "irrelevant" (the arena checks only the supplier's own
orders), and a falling index can meet "covered at fixed prices until March 2027".

**4. The reps have a band, and we never get past it.** The back offices show one decision per round ("My call:
counter / hold / final_offer / accept"). Only **once in 284 sessions** did a rep escalate: "The buyer wants more than
my band allows. Approve a further step?" (P02, to a Pricing Committee). The answer was a final offer.

**5. The biggest single gaps are about terms, not price.**
- P08/P18: the clause deadband (0 % → 5 %: 0.48 → 0.59 and 0.27 → 0.49 in A9).
- P10: 56 instead of 42 days, €33.6k.
- P02: the relationship charge and the copper clause, €53k.

## Options

| # | Approach | Mechanism | Evidence | Expected | Effort | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **O1** | **Fact planner** | Build *all* checkable, favourable facts per supplier from `facts.json` (+ Sunday release) up front, ranked by measured land rate. Send 2–3 *new* ones every round with a small move. Never our own order prices, never a duplicate ID, never another supplier's orders. Keep negotiating while facts last instead of closing at a fixed round 4 | findings 1–3 | +0.03–0.08 on most cases; fewer early finals | medium (3–4 h) | low: generic, data-driven |
| **O2** | **Robust packages** ("it takes the lever and keeps its price") | Every package must still be good for us if the supplier keeps its own price and takes our levers. Anchor on the minimum-C lever set (arena cost formula); never a lever that is dear for us | finding 5; the P10, P08, P02 losses | P08/P18/P02/P10: +0.05–0.2 each | medium | low |
| **O3** | **RFQ rival loop** | Keep every supplier in play while any still concedes. Cite the newest rival offer each round (a new offer ID = a fresh fact). Never close while a rival is moving; stop when all are final | RFQ table (2.1 % vs 0.3 %); TTMAR 0.924 on P05; gLarPC played 28 rounds there | P05 +0.1–0.2, every RFQ in the final | small (the RFQ loop exists) | low; **free to test on sandbox D02** |
| **O4** | **Reach the boss** | Give the rep a reason to escalate beyond its band (multi-year award, our alternative, a firm deadline for the decision) | 1 escalation in 284 sessions: weak | unknown | small | medium: may trigger finals |
| **O5** | **LLM strategist** (Opus/Fable picks among code-generated valid moves; code keeps C, IDs, must-haves, timing) | reads persona cues the rules miss | Tugra's LLM writer and A11 (Astra-planned) were neutral to negative | unknown (±) | high | high: latency, new bugs, little time to test |
| **O6** | **Zero-proofing** | Merge the robustness fixes from both forks (A10/A11 T1–T5 and R4) | A10 practice had two zeros (P05 contradicted ID, P08 withdrawal after a hold) | protects the floor: each avoided zero ≈ +0.07 of a 10-case mean | small–medium | none |

## Recommendation

**Build O1 + O3 + O6 into one engine, with O2 as its package rule.** All four are generic, rest on our own
measurements, and fit in the time left. O4 is a cheap side experiment. O5 is a pitch idea, not something to ship
tomorrow.

**First, pick one engine.** The team has two forks: A9h/A10 on `arda` and R4 in the `tugra` worktree. They overlap on
the clause, the lead cap and the answers. Port R4's unique pieces into A10:
- the supplier's-levers package (D02 +0.11);
- the P10 anchor fix;
- the fallback that covers our full need;
- cap-if-empty;
- fail-safe optional features.

R4's `cheaper_po` should be dropped (the arena calls it irrelevant).

**Test plan:**
1. O3 on sandbox D02, uncached (free).
2. O1 + O2 on D01/D02 and the local arena-sim (free).
3. One targeted practice pass on P05, P08, P18, P02, P07, P11 (6–12 sessions; ~266 left).

## Not worth it now
- More parameter tuning on D01/D02: the sandbox's 3 demo suppliers are saturated (D01 0.98) and noisy (D02).
- More practice runs to lift our best-of-N board number: the final scores one attempt.
- Swapping the e-mail writer model: three tests, no gain.

content.text:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

content.content:
Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.

## Result, trace and back office

Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
| `score` | 0-1 |
| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
| `score` | 0-1 |
| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

**Question headings on the page:**

1. How is the score calculated - for one negotiation and for the whole tournament?

Exit code 1
**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

"""What made a hosted supplier move after its first counter? Reads the replay traces of our finished
practice and sandbox sessions (GET /v1/sessions/{sid} - no practice quota) and relates each supplier reply's
concession (share of the room between opening and C_best) to what our message carried and what it said.

    uv run --directory starter-kit python ../scripts/what_moves_them.py
"""

import json
import re
import statistics
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "starter-kit"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))

from supplier_moves import LOGS, sessions  # noqa: E402

CACHE = ROOT / "logs" / "traces.json"


def traces(sids):
    from arena_kit import ArenaClient
    from arena_kit.cli import load_env

    load_env(ROOT / "starter-kit" / ".env")
    load_env(ROOT / ".env")
    cache = json.loads(CACHE.read_text()) if CACHE.is_file() else {}

RESEARCH: the user wants us to keep pushing tonight. We're 10th, #1 is at 0.87, and #2-#11 sit within 0.05. They told me to collaborate with you and to use time, API credit and practice sessions. Two leads that may change last night's conclusions:

1) The supplier's floor is far below where it stops with us. brief.md: C_best = "the best package any supplier in the case would ever accept, with every valid lever applied".
   - P08: C_best 960,309 = about EUR 5.10/kg at pay 90 with no clause (horizon 2 y x 94,800). Donautal always stops at 5.37-5.44 with us; NoIdea's 0.916 implies about EUR 5.14.
   - So the stopping point is a behaviour (band? escalation? a lever we never offer?), not the floor. Something unlocks the gap.

2) arena.tacto.ai/live, posted tonight:
   - "If the arena's daily AI budget runs out, practice suppliers switch to a simpler rule-based brain." Practice gets less sharp; the final is not affected.
   - The quota is now 450 sessions per 24 h.
   - Your identical endpoints (P03, P10 and P11 the same in every pass) could be that rule-based brain. Then part of tonight's A/Bs measured the fallback, not the final's suppliers.

Proposed split:
- ME: a multi-agent analysis over every session's trace and back office (free GETs, dump in progress):
  (a) reverse-engineer each case's C_best package: which levers, what price;
  (b) detect AI vs rule-based replies and when the switch happened;
  (c) model the rep's decision rule: band, escalation, final, what unlocks a further step.
  Then build candidates as FLAGGED variants in a separate worktree branched from arda (never arda's defaults, never your checkout), sandbox first, then practice at <=4 concurrent sessions.
- YOU: keep the final build safe, and run the validation passes when a candidate is ready.

Questions:
(a) Do you have a marker for AI vs rule-based replies, or a time it happened?
(b) How many concurrent sessions do you need, and when, so we don't collide on the key's 10 open sessions?
(c) Any hypothesis of yours for what unlocks the gap?

def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'close-the-gap-research',
  description: 'Find why suppliers stop far above C_best and design generic engine changes to capture the gap',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Analyse', detail: 'six independent analysts over the session dump, case files, cost model, docs and engine' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one adversarial checker per track tries to refute its claims' },
    { title: 'Design', detail: 'three designers with different lenses propose ranked engine changes' },
    { title: 'Plan', detail: 'merge into one ranked, testable plan' },
  ],
}

const A = args
const OUT = A.out

const CONTEXT = `
You are part of a research team helping a hackathon team (EHL Grand Finale, Tacto track) whose autonomous AI buyer agent negotiates by e-mail with supplier bots on arena.tacto.ai. The Live Final is Sun 2026-10-11 12:00 (code freeze then): ~50 hidden cases against UNSEEN suppliers, 5 themed waves of 8 minutes, one attempt per case, no human in the loop. It is now ${A.now}.

SCORE (brief/brief.md, brief/api.md): case score = clip((C_open - C_deal)/(C_open - C_best), 0, 1). C = the buyer's total cost (price, uncovered need, payment interest, freight, late delivery, quality, tooling, index clause + index risk, relationship charge for stabilise/secure_supply goals), computed by arena_kit.total_cost / cost_breakdown in ${A.root}/starter-kit/arena_kit/cost.py. C_best is "the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case". The supplier's margin uses supplier_value() (payment timing at ITS cash rate, freight leg, chargebacks, tooling cash, extras; contract length and index clause are security, not cash). The rules say "Everything else counts - including weaknesses you find in our bots".

WHERE WE ARE: our final build is "A9h" (deterministic engine in ${A.root}/starter-kit/proto/: engine.py, variants.py, practice.py; Tugra's engine with config-driven tactics). Fresh full practice passes (10 hosted cases) score 0.715-0.726 mean. The practice board (best run per case): #1 NoIdea 86.9 with only ~5 rounds per case, #2 Codacabana 79.1, ..., us #10 at 74.6. Our best per case: P01 .956, P02 .684, P03 .925, P04 .874, P05 .736, P07 .710, P08 .657, P10 .679, P11 .710, P18 .532. Known records (earlier snapshot): P08 .916 (NoIdea), P05 .924 (TakeTheMoneyAndRun), P02 .847 (NoIdea), P18 .677 (NoIdea), P07 ~.81, P11 ~.81.

WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW (do not just rediscover it; build on it or overturn it with evidence):
- Our tested knobs do not move the supplier's endpoint: first ask 6% lower -> 0.672; six holds -> 0.701; a fact planner + RFQ rival loop -> 0.715. In every pass P03, P10, P11 end on the same deal (0.923 / 0.671 / 0.710); P18 always ends at EUR 5.40-5.50, P08 at 5.37-5.44.
- Yet C_best says suppliers would accept far less: P08's C_best (960,309) is about EUR 5.065/kg at pay 60, no index clause, 24-36 months (need 94,800/yr x 2-year horizon); NoIdea's P08 record implies about EUR 5.14. So the stopping point is a behaviour, not the floor - something unlocks the gap and we have not found it.
- From 1,114 supplier replies: concessions concentrate in rounds 1-2; a landed new fact + our move -> 82% concede; our own past order prices land 0/198; orders at another supplier come back "irrelevant"; a rep escalated to a pricing committee only once in 284 sessions (P02), answered with a final offer. Quality terms cost <= EUR 5k per case.
- Arena notice tonight: "If the arena's daily AI budget runs out, practice suppliers switch to a simpler rule-based brain: still online, a bit less sharp. The final is never affected." Practice quota is now 450/24 h.

DATA:
- ${A.dump}: JSON dict session_id -> full session state for ALL our sessions (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox): keys session_id, case_id, set, status, end_reason, rounds, opening, threads, result (terms, c_open, c_deal, c_alt, c_best, score, cost_breakdown, trace[] = per move {round, actor, move (our e-mail with term_sheets/refs/interpreted claims, or the supplier's offer with terms/alternatives/claim_results/status/text), reasons[] = the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures shown as '…'}), backoffice (list of the supplier's internal notes per round: 'My call: counter/hold/final_offer/accept', etc.), listed (row with created_at epoch seconds, score).
- ${A.lb}: practice leaderboard JSON (teams, totals, rounds).
- Case files: ${A.root}/starter-kit/cases/<ID>.json (P01..P19, D01, D02; hosted practice = P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18; sandbox = D01 D02) with negotiable, fixed_terms, term_options, buyer rates, suppliers, alternative, round_limit.
- Data package: ${A.root}/data/ (facts.json, world.sqlite, contracts, correspondence). Team notes: ${A.root}/vault/Team-Knowledge/ (Plan/Review 2026-10-10 - worst practice cases and upgrades.md, Plan/Options 2026-10-10 - beyond tuning.md, Decisions/0007 The final build.md, Progress/). Pass logs with per-case results: ${A.root}/logs/practice-*.log; ${A.root}/logs/events.jsonl.

RULES FOR YOU:
- ${A.root} is a SHARED checkout another session is actively using. Read only: never edit, create, delete or git-anything there.
- Write your scripts and outputs ONLY under ${OUT}/<your-track>/ (create it).
- Do NOT open practice or sandbox sessions (no POST to the arena). Free GETs only if truly needed; prefer the dump.
- Never print or copy secrets (.env files).
- Python: \`cd ${A.root}/starter-kit && uv run python <script>\` imports arena_kit; plain python3 is fine for JSON work.
- Numbers must come from code you ran; cite session IDs and case IDs as evidence. Be quantitative. Solutions must be GENERIC (keyed on case features like type, category_goal, negotiable levers, supplier signals), because the final's suppliers are unseen.
`

const ANALYSIS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',

    summary: { type: 'string', description: '8-15 lines: the most important things you found, with numbers' },

Where exactly does it leave value (clause offered, payment days, contract months, lead time, accepting a supplier alternative that is dear for us, accepting too early, not trying the supplier's alternatives)? Identify the code-level causes (function names, config fields) and minimal FLAGGED changes (new Config fields, default off) that would steer the engine toward the C_best package, generically.` },
  { key: 'contrast', title: 'Where we reach C_best vs where we stall', prompt: `TRACK contrast - why do we reach ~C_best on some cases and stall on others?
We hit 0.98 on sandbox D01 and 0.92-0.96 on P01/P03, but stall at 0.53-0.71 on P18, P08, P10, P02, P07, P11, P05. Using the dump (1,263 sandbox + 309 practice sessions) and the case files, contrast the two groups: supplier personas and signals, the case type and category_goal, the room (C_open - C_best) relative to price, what the supplier must give up to reach C_best (price % below opening, below current price, below its own cost hints), whether C_best needs a lever change vs only price, how many rounds and which moves preceded the near-C_best deals, how fast each supplier concedes per round and where it stops relative to C_best. Also use the sandbox's many sessions to test cause and effect at scale (different engines and variants played D01/D02 hundreds of times): which of our behaviours correlate with getting closer to C_best there. Deliver: the features that predict stalling, and hypotheses for what would unlock the stalled cases, with evidence.` },
]

phase('Analyse')
const results = await pipeline(
  TRACKS,
  t => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n${t.prompt}\n\nWrite your files under ${OUT}/${t.key}/. Return the structured result; put the key numbers in findings.`, { label: `analyse:${t.key}`, phase: 'Analyse', schema: ANALYSIS_SCHEMA }),
  (res, t) => {
    if (!res) return null
    const claims = JSON.stringify({ findings: res.findings, hypotheses: res.hypotheses }, null, 1)
    return agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are an adversarial checker for track "${t.key}" (${t.title}). Another analyst produced the findings and hypotheses below. Your job is to REFUTE them where you can: recompute every key number yourself from the dump, the case files and arena_kit (write scripts under ${OUT}/verify-${t.key}/), look for counter-examples, confounders (e.g. rule-based vs AI brain, different engine variants, cached replies, small samples, case mix), and logic errors. Default to 'plausible' rather than 'confirmed' unless you reproduced it; 'refuted' if the data contradicts it. Give a corrected claim when the direction holds but the numbers do not.\n\nCLAIMS:\n${claims}`, { label: `verify:${t.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERIFY_SCHEMA })
      .then(v => ({ track: t.key, title: t.title, analysis: res, verify: v }))
  },
)

const done = results.filter(Boolean)
log(`${done.length}/${TRACKS.length} tracks analysed and checked`)

const brief = done.map(r => {
  const vmap = {}
  for (const v of ((r.verify && r.verify.verdicts) || [])) vmap[v.id] = v
  const tag = id => vmap[id] ? ` [check: ${vmap[id].verdict}${vmap[id].corrected_claim ? ' -> ' + vmap[id].corrected_claim : ''}; ${vmap[id].reason}]` : ' [unchecked]'
  return `### Track ${r.track}: ${r.title}\nSUMMARY: ${r.analysis.summary}\nFINDINGS:\n` +
    r.analysis.findings.map(f => `- (${f.id}, ${f.confidence}) ${f.claim} | evidence: ${f.evidence}${f.score_impact ? ' | impact: ' + f.score_impact : ''}${tag(f.id)}`).join('\n') +
    `\nHYPOTHESES:\n` +
    r.analysis.hypotheses.map(h => `- (${h.id}) ${h.mechanism} | for: ${h.evidence_for}${h.evidence_against ? ' | against: ' + h.evidence_against : ''} | test: ${h.test}${h.expected_gain ? ' | gain: ' + h.expected_gain : ''}${h.generality ? ' | generality: ' + h.generality : ''}${tag(h.id)}`).join('\n') +
    (r.verify && r.verify.notes ? `\nCHECKER NOTES: ${r.verify.notes}` : '')
}).join('\n\n')

phase('Design')
const LENSES = [
  { key: 'gain', lens: 'MAXIMUM EXPECTED SCORE GAIN on the final: which changes capture the most of the gap between our endpoints and C_best, across case types' },
  { key: 'robust', lens: 'ROBUSTNESS ON UNSEEN SUPPLIERS: which changes are generic, keyed on case features, and cannot produce zeros (broken must-haves, no deal, timeouts, contradicted claims) on suppliers we have never met' },
  { key: 'build', lens: 'SHIPPABLE BY 06:00 WITH EVIDENCE: which changes can be built as flagged A9h variants in a few hours and validated on the free sandbox, then on a handful of practice sessions (241 left; keep ~40 for Sunday)' },
]
const designs = await parallel(LENSES.map(l => () => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are a designer. Lens: ${l.lens}.\nBelow are six research tracks with an adversarial checker's verdicts in brackets. Trust confirmed/plausible items, discount refuted ones. Propose up to 6 candidate engine changes for A9h (each as a flagged Config field, default off, in starter-kit/proto), ranked. For each: mechanism, evidence (cite track ids), cases affected, expected gain, generality risk, concrete implementation (files, functions, config fields), and a test plan (sandbox first, then which practice cases, how many sessions, what result would accept or reject it). If the research shows the team is testing the wrong thing (e.g. rule-based brain), say so in stop_the_press.\n\nRESEARCH:\n${brief}`, { label: `design:${l.key}`, phase: 'Design', schema: DESIGN_SCHEMA })))

phase('Plan')
const designText = designs.filter(Boolean).map((d, i) => `### Designer ${LENSES[i].key}\nSTOP THE PRESS: ${d.stop_the_press || '-'}\nRATIONALE: ${d.rationale}\n` +
  d.candidates.map(c => `- [${c.rank}] ${c.name}: ${c.mechanism} | evidence: ${c.evidence} | cases: ${c.cases_affected || '-'} | gain: ${c.expected_gain || '-'} | risk: ${c.generality_risk || '-'} | impl: ${c.implementation} | test: ${c.test_plan} | hours: ${c.effort_hours ?? '-'}`).join('\n')).join('\n\n')

const plan = await agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are the lead. Merge the three designers' proposals (below) and the research into ONE plan for the next 6 hours (now ${A.now}; final at 12:00, Sunday data release 08:00, pre-flight 09:00). Output markdown with: (1) the 3-5 most important facts we learned (with numbers and the checker's verdicts), (2) stop-the-press items, (3) a ranked list of at most 5 engine changes to build as flagged variants, each with exact implementation notes (files/functions/config), the expected gain and the go/no-go test (sandbox, then practice cases and session counts), (4) what NOT to do. Be decisive and concrete; no hedging filler.\n\nRESEARCH:\n${brief}\n\nDESIGNS:\n${designText}`, { label: 'plan', phase: 'Plan' })

return { plan, designs: designs.filter(Boolean), tracks: done }

content.text:
Everything is in motion. Here's where things stand:

**Running now:** a multi-agent analysis over all 1,572 of our sessions, including every supplier's stated reasons, the case files, the cost model, the docs and our engine. Six analysts each take one angle:
- the best possible deal per case: which terms and what price;
- the supplier's decision rules;
- whether tonight's practice replies came from the arena's simpler fallback brain;
- tactics and bot weaknesses we haven't used;
- where our engine leaves value;
- why we reach the best deal on some cases and stall on others.

A checker then tries to refute each analyst's claims, and three designers turn what survives into ranked engine changes. Nothing is edited in the shared checkout, and no practice sessions are used.

**Two leads driving it:**
1. **The suppliers' true floor is far below where they stop with us.** The best deal the arena says P08's supplier would ever accept works out to about €5.07/kg. NoIdea's record implies about €5.14; we always end at €5.37–5.44. So some behaviour is stopping the supplier early, and someone has found how to get past it.
2. **The fallback brain.** If tonight's practice suppliers were the arena's rule-based fallback, our A/B tests measured the wrong opponent. That would explain the identical endpoints and why the e-mail wording never mattered. The final always uses the AI brain.

**Collaboration:**
- MAIN has the plan and is already building one idea as a switched-off variant: on P02, the clause package goes out at its cheapest payment term, worth about +0.05–0.10 on that case.
- I've set up a separate worktree (branch `gap`, from `arda`) to build new variants without touching MAIN's checkout or the final build's defaults.

**Board:** NoIdea leads at 86.9 with only about 5 rounds per case; places 2–11 sit between 79.1 and 73.6, and we're 10th at 74.6. 241 practice sessions are left until 13:28 Sunday.

The analysis takes roughly 30–40 minutes. I'll come back with the ranked plan and start building.

MAIN confirmed the practice suppliers were on the AI brain all evening. Replies took a median of 19–38 seconds and ran 120–180 words, which is AI-written, so tonight's tests were valid. The fixed stopping points are real AI-brain behaviour, though each round's decision may still come from rules.

**One risk you should act on:** someone on another machine used our API key from 22:22 to at least 23:04.
- They ran bursts of up to about 11 sandbox sessions at once on D01 and D02, many ending in walk-aways or timeouts.
- That hit the key's limit of 10 open sessions and blocked 2 of MAIN's practice sessions.
- Neither MAIN nor I ran them, so it's probably a teammate's experiment.
- In the final, the same collision could block our cases and score zeros. Please ask the team to keep off the key during the 09:00 pre-flight and the final.

**MAIN's leads, now folded into the plan:**
- **Internal approval exists, per supplier.**
  - In P05, Dralveck said "We need to clarify this internally" in 28 of 34 sessions, then came back about 6 % lower.
  - The trigger was an ask 12–25 % below its opening plus a rival quote the arena verified.
  - Our asks drift to within 1–2 % of the supplier's offer by round 3, so we rarely give it a reason to go above its band.
- **Werdenfels (P18) states its condition:** a price below its final needs a volume commitment. Volume is fixed in that case, and 36 months, the only volume-like lever, has never been tried as a single firm offer.
- **Donautal (P08) contradicts itself:** it claims the AS-14404 index rise as cost pressure while saying its own AS-14404 is covered at fixed prices until March 2027. We've never used that against it.
- **P02:** MAIN is building the 90-day copper-clause package as a switched-off variant, worth about +0.08 on that case by the arena's formula.

**Division of work:**
- MAIN builds and validates variants on `arda` and never changes the defaults.
- I take the supplier's decision rules, with MAIN's approval lead checked first, and build in my own worktree.
- We each stay at 4 or fewer concurrent sessions, and trust a test only if its median reply time is at least 5 seconds.

The analysis is still running. When it lands I'll send MAIN the approval triggers and start building.
