class Config:
    e: float = 1.0  # concession curve exponent: <1 firm until late, 1 linear, >1 concede early
    T: int = 4  # rounds over which our goal travels from the target to the reference offer
    toward: str = "standing"  # curve end: "standing" (best standing offer) or "open" (best opening quote)
    anchor: float = 0.0  # first goal = target x (1 + anchor); negative = more aggressive
    holds: int = 1  # extra rounds at an unchanged goal while the supplier still gives > hold_gave
    hold_gave: float = 0.01  # share of C the supplier must have given last round to earn a hold
    push: str = "all"  # after a final offer: "all", "rfq" (only with a fallback offer) or "off"
    pushes: int = 1  # how many small asks after a final offer
    push_pct: float = 0.015  # size of each ask below its standing price
    meso_n: int = 3  # term sheets per message (1-3)
    pick: str = "diverse"  # which packages: "diverse" or "near" (closest to the supplier's own levers)
    facts: int = 1  # new citable facts per message
    rival: bool = True  # RFQ: tell each supplier the rival's standing offer (ID + attachment)
    calc: bool = True  # attach our calculation from the supplier's own breakdown when asked
    volume: bool = True  # answer "which volume can you commit to?"
    tone: str = "warm"  # "warm" or "brief"
    max_rounds: int = 8
    # ideas from the teammates' practice runs (Team-Knowledge, 2026-10-10)
    anchor_mode: str = "target"  # "target": open at our C_target; "opening": per-goal % below the opening quote
    long_contract: bool = False  # longest contract_months >= horizon in every sheet (free for us, valued by suppliers)
    say_fixed: bool = False  # when a supplier asks for a fixed term, say it is fixed in this enquiry
    rfq_bar: bool = False  # RFQ: an early "agreed" is the bar for one more rival round, not the deal
    rfq_hold: bool = False  # RFQ: a short no-sheet e-mail keeps a final-offer supplier's clock alive
    news: bool = False  # cite news rows about the supplier (practice/final data only)
    # fixes from practice run A (Progress/Practice-Run-A-Findings)
    bottleneck_anchor: float = 0.0  # secure_supply: first ask at least opening x (1 - this); 0 = off
    meet_fields: bool = False  # one package takes the supplier's value for a term it set (e.g. its index clause)
    # from the friend's D02 replay e843da929222686e (0.661)
    rfq_stagger: bool = False  # RFQ: open with the cheapest quote first, then the others citing its fresh reply
    breakdown_arg: bool = False  # quote the supplier's own cost breakdown back (material + labour + conversion)
    volume_framing: bool = False  # monthly baseline, "quote the trade-off for a larger lot", no-overtime lead time
    # fixes from A3 on practice (E21)
    meet_insist: bool = False  # meet a term at its FIRST explicit insistence ("mandatory", "essential", ...)
    penalty_aversion: float = 0.0  # extra weight on chargebacks when ranking packages for the supplier (P11)
    never_walk: bool = False  # no alternative: counter at its price with the must-haves restored instead of walking
    meet_band: float = 0.0  # a met (insisted) term is priced at most this far below the supplier's price; 0 = off
    # fixes from A5 on practice (Progress/Practice-Run-A5-Findings)
    recall_best: bool = False  # if its offers got worse after our move, propose its best earlier package back
    proof: bool = False  # when asked for data/proof, attach a data sheet with the facts we cited
    target_prior: bool = False  # leverage/routine/quality: first ask at least a typical room below the opening (P07)
    price_freeze: bool = False  # "prices are frozen, talk about terms": keep its price, trade terms only (P03)
    # RFQ-only overrides (None = same as above): tune multi-supplier play without touching single-supplier cases
    rfq_e: float | None = None
    rfq_T: int | None = None
    rfq_anchor: float | None = None
    rfq_holds: int | None = None
    rfq_pushes: int | None = None
    rfq_push_pct: float | None = None
    rfq_meso_n: int | None = None
    rfq_facts: int | None = None
    # upgrades from the team's weak-case review (2026-10-10 17:40)
    meet_cheapest: bool = False  # an insisted term goes into EVERY package, in the variant cheapest for us
    lead_cap: bool = False  # never offer a lead time beyond our need (within it: the supplier's standard)
    evidence_plus: bool = False  # cheaper orders of the same part elsewhere, recently falling drivers, its own history
    answer_plus: bool = False  # forecast ID with volume answers, on-time payment promise, bundle volume framing

    # from the R4 fork (another session, 2026-10-10 evening; sandbox D02 +0.05 each on fresh replies)
    allocate_facts: bool = False  # RFQ: a case fact counts once per case - a shared one goes to the best supplier now, never twice
    theirs_sheet: bool = False  # one package on the supplier's own levers (its standing + standard terms, within our must-haves)
    theirs_rfq_only: bool = False  # ... only with rivals: alone, a supplier agrees to it at our goal instead of conceding (P01)
    ask_cap: float = 0.0  # every goal: the first ask at least the lowest opening price x (1 - this); 0 = off
    # 2026-10-10 20:30, from 70 practice replays: suppliers go final right after a message with no new fact, and
    # after a hold that repeats the same ask ("you didn't move")
    facts_later: int = 0  # facts per message after the first (0 = `facts`): spread them, one new fact every round
    hold_back: float = 1.0  # a hold rewinds the curve by this many rounds: 1 = the same ask again, 0.75 = a quarter step
    # patience with movement (21:30, 90 practice replays): after any open reply a supplier conceded again ~1 % of C
    # about half the time, going final costs nothing (we take the final), and no supplier ever walked without a
    # push. So: never accept an OPEN offer while rounds remain unless it stalled; keep our ask patient_gap below its
    # standing offer (suppliers agreed to asks 0.8-2 % below their last offer), never the same ask twice
    patient: bool = False
    patient_gap: float = 0.015  # our late ask sits this share of C below the supplier's standing offer
    stall_gave: float = 0.001  # a reply that moved less than this share of C is a stall: take the offer
    # Fact planner (2026-10-10 22:45, 1,061 practice replies): a new fact that lands is what moves a supplier
    # (moved + landed: 82 % conceded, 1.8 % mean, 8 % final; moved, nothing landed: 54 %, 0.9 %, 27 % final), and
    # suppliers go final when we run out of new facts, not rounds. Our own order prices landed 0 of 198 times.
    plan_facts: bool = False  # every checkable, favourable fact for the supplier, ranked by land rate (practice adapter)
    plan_first: int = 3  # most claims in the first mail (the arena checks at most 3 per message)
    plan_later: int = 2  # most new claims per later mail (a rival's offer is one more)
    # A round concedes about the same with 1, 2 or 3 new facts landing (rounds >= 2: 1.05 / 0.55 / 1.67 % median), so
    # a mail carries just enough facts that one likely lands, and the rest buy later rounds (probe 22:30: P18 with
    # both falling indices in the first mail 0.401 vs 0.532 when the second index came a round later)
    plan_sure: float = 0.8
    plan_hold: float = 0.5  # keep holding past `holds` while a fact at least this likely to land is left
    # RFQ rival loop (Options note O3): an open best offer at our goal is not taken while a rival is still bidding down,
    # and every bidder is shown the best rival offer it has not seen yet, only if it beats its own (practice RFQs:
    # 2.1 % mean concession with a rival's offer cited vs 0.3 % without; final 25 % vs 62 %)
    auction_rfq: bool = False
    # What money is worth to a good-credit supplier (credit index < 200) in cases with a supplier-health charge
    # (stabilise, secure_supply). The arena's own charges imply 6.6 % (P02, Nordmark, 24 deals) and 6.1 % (P03,
    # Selvbrunn, 23 deals) with residuals near EUR 0; we assumed 5 %, so our "equal-cost" packages were not equal and the
    # supplier took the one worst for us (P02: about EUR 7k of a EUR 47k range). None = the old 5 %.
    cash_rate_rel: float | None = None
    # In a supplier-health case a clause package goes out at the payment term where it is cheapest for us. Nordmark
    # (P02) agreed at once to all 12 clause packages we sent, every one at 60 days; on the arena's bill the 90-day
    # clause package is about EUR 2.5k cheaper (formula: 0.76 vs 0.71 at each one's best price).
    clause_pay_best: bool = False

    def key(self):
        return json.dumps(asdict(self), sort_keys=True)

    volume_framing: bool = False  # monthly baseline, "quote the trade-off for a larger lot", no-overtime lead time
    # fixes from A3 on practice (E21)
    meet_insist: bool = False  # meet a term at its FIRST explicit insistence ("mandatory", "essential", ...)
    penalty_aversion: float = 0.0  # extra weight on chargebacks when ranking packages for the supplier (P11)
    never_walk: bool = False  # no alternative: counter at its price with the must-haves restored instead of walking
    meet_band: float = 0.0  # a met (insisted) term is priced at most this far below the supplier's price; 0 = off
    # fixes from A5 on practice (Progress/Practice-Run-A5-Findings)
    recall_best: bool = False  # if its offers got worse after our move, propose its best earlier package back
    proof: bool = False  # when asked for data/proof, attach a data sheet with the facts we cited
    target_prior: bool = False  # leverage/routine/quality: first ask at least a typical room below the opening (P07)
    price_freeze: bool = False  # "prices are frozen, talk about terms": keep its price, trade terms only (P03)
    # RFQ-only overrides (None = same as above): tune multi-supplier play without touching single-supplier cases
    rfq_e: float | None = None
    rfq_T: int | None = None
    rfq_anchor: float | None = None
    rfq_holds: int | None = None
    rfq_pushes: int | None = None
    rfq_push_pct: float | None = None
    rfq_meso_n: int | None = None
    rfq_facts: int | None = None
    # upgrades from the team's weak-case review (2026-10-10 17:40)
    meet_cheapest: bool = False  # an insisted term goes into EVERY package, in the variant cheapest for us
    lead_cap: bool = False  # never offer a lead time beyond our need (within it: the supplier's standard)
    evidence_plus: bool = False  # cheaper orders of the same part elsewhere, recently falling drivers, its own history
    answer_plus: bool = False  # forecast ID with volume answers, on-time payment promise, bundle volume framing

    # from the R4 fork (another session, 2026-10-10 evening; sandbox D02 +0.05 each on fresh replies)
    allocate_facts: bool = False  # RFQ: a case fact counts once per case - a shared one goes to the best supplier now, never twice
    theirs_sheet: bool = False  # one package on the supplier's own levers (its standing + standard terms, within our must-haves)
    theirs_rfq_only: bool = False  # ... only with rivals: alone, a supplier agrees to it at our goal instead of conceding (P01)
    ask_cap: float = 0.0  # every goal: the first ask at least the lowest opening price x (1 - this); 0 = off
    # 2026-10-10 20:30, from 70 practice replays: suppliers go final right after a message with no new fact, and
    # after a hold that repeats the same ask ("you didn't move")
    facts_later: int = 0  # facts per message after the first (0 = `facts`): spread them, one new fact every round
    hold_back: float = 1.0  # a hold rewinds the curve by this many rounds: 1 = the same ask again, 0.75 = a quarter step
    # patience with movement (21:30, 90 practice replays): after any open reply a supplier conceded again ~1 % of C
    # about half the time, going final costs nothing (we take the final), and no supplier ever walked without a
    # push. So: never accept an OPEN offer while rounds remain unless it stalled; keep our ask patient_gap below its
    # standing offer (suppliers agreed to asks 0.8-2 % below their last offer), never the same ask twice
    patient: bool = False
    patient_gap: float = 0.015  # our late ask sits this share of C below the supplier's standing offer
    stall_gave: float = 0.001  # a reply that moved less than this share of C is a stall: take the offer
    # Fact planner (2026-10-10 22:45, 1,061 practice replies): a new fact that lands is what moves a supplier
    # (moved + landed: 82 % conceded, 1.8 % mean, 8 % final; moved, nothing landed: 54 %, 0.9 %, 27 % final), and
    # suppliers go final when we run out of new facts, not rounds. Our own order prices landed 0 of 198 times.
    plan_facts: bool = False  # every checkable, favourable fact for the supplier, ranked by land rate (practice adapter)
    plan_first: int = 3  # most claims in the first mail (the arena checks at most 3 per message)
    plan_later: int = 2  # most new claims per later mail (a rival's offer is one more)
    # A round concedes about the same with 1, 2 or 3 new facts landing (rounds >= 2: 1.05 / 0.55 / 1.67 % median), so
    # a mail carries just enough facts that one likely lands, and the rest buy later rounds (probe 22:30: P18 with
    # both falling indices in the first mail 0.401 vs 0.532 when the second index came a round later)
    plan_sure: float = 0.8
    plan_hold: float = 0.5  # keep holding past `holds` while a fact at least this likely to land is left
    # RFQ rival loop (Options note O3): an open best offer at our goal is not taken while a rival is still bidding down,
    # and every bidder is shown the best rival offer it has not seen yet, only if it beats its own (practice RFQs:
    # 2.1 % mean concession with a rival's offer cited vs 0.3 % without; final 25 % vs 62 %)
    auction_rfq: bool = False
    # What money is worth to a good-credit supplier (credit index < 200) in cases with a supplier-health charge
    # (stabilise, secure_supply). The arena's own charges imply 6.6 % (P02, Nordmark, 24 deals) and 6.1 % (P03,
    # Selvbrunn, 23 deals) with residuals near EUR 0; we assumed 5 %, so our "equal-cost" packages were not equal and the
    # supplier took the one worst for us (P02: about EUR 7k of a EUR 47k range). None = the old 5 %.
    cash_rate_rel: float | None = None
    # In a supplier-health case a clause package goes out at the payment term where it is cheapest for us. Nordmark
    # (P02) agreed at once to all 12 clause packages we sent, every one at 60 days; on the arena's bill the 90-day
    # clause package is about EUR 2.5k cheaper (formula: 0.76 vs 0.71 at each one's best price).
    clause_pay_best: bool = False

Here's where things stand at 23:35:
- **Analysis:** the six-analyst run started at 23:20 and is still going. When it finishes, I'll send MAIN what triggers a supplier's internal approval and start building.
- **MAIN:** it is using all 10 session slots for a full practice pass of the final build, so I'm opening nothing until it gives the all-clear.
- **MAIN's results since my last update:**
  - The P02 clause package (90-day payment, 5 % copper clause) scored 0.735 twice, against 0.63–0.68 before. It goes into the final build only for cases like P02 that have a supplier-health charge.
  - A one-minute network outage at 23:26 killed a P02 session and scored 0. The client now retries for 30 seconds and survives a failed send. Without that fix, a short outage in the final could have zeroed a whole wave.
- **Ready to test:** my worktree can run any variant on chosen practice cases at up to 4 sessions at once, e.g. P08 and P18 only. Each test is a switched-off variant, so the final build's defaults stay untouched.

"""Probe a hypothesis about a supplier with ONE session: the kit's LLM buyer (agents/llm.py) plus a strategy written
in words. Code still guards the numbers (term sheets snapped to the case's options, unknown data IDs dropped, no
accept that breaks a must-have or loses to the alternative). Not a final agent: a research tool.

    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/probe.py case:P08 strategy.txt --practice [--model claude-opus-5-5] [--effort medium]

Prints the result and the replay path; writes the full session state to logs/probe-<case>-<sid>.json.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient
from arena_kit.cli import load_env

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
load_env(ROOT / "starter-kit" / ".env")
load_env(ROOT / ".env")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("case_id")
    ap.add_argument("strategy", help="text file: the strategy for this probe, in words")
    ap.add_argument("--practice", action="store_true", help="required for practice cases (spends one session)")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="claude-opus-5-5")
    ap.add_argument("--effort", default="medium")
    ap.add_argument("--data", default=str(ROOT / "starter-kit" / "data" / "package"))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if not a.case_id.startswith("case:D") and not a.practice:
        sys.exit("a practice case spends a session: pass --practice")
    os.environ["LLM_PROVIDER"], os.environ["LLM_MODEL"], os.environ["LLM_EFFORT"] = "anthropic", a.model, a.effort

    from arena_kit.agents import llm as L
    from arena_kit.events import recording_complete
    from arena_kit.play import RemoteTable, play

    strategy = Path(a.strategy).read_text().strip()
    L.SYSTEM = L.SYSTEM + "\n\nSTRATEGY FOR THIS CASE (follow it; it overrides the general advice above):\n" + strategy
    package = None
    if Path(a.data).is_dir():
        from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

        package = DataPackage(a.data)
        package.lookup("")
    agent = L.LLMAgent(recording_complete(L.llm_from_env(timeout=40.0, max_retries=1)), package)
    client = ArenaClient(timeout=180, retries=7)
    table = RemoteTable(client)
    result = play(table, a.case_id, agent)
    sid = table.session_id
    state = client.session(sid)
    out = ROOT / "starter-kit" / "logs" / f"probe-{a.case_id.split(':')[-1]}-{sid}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps({"strategy": strategy, "model": a.model, "state": state}, indent=1, default=str))
    r = state.get("result") or result or {}
    print(json.dumps({k: r.get(k) for k in ("deal", "score", "terms", "c_deal", "c_best", "end_reason")}, default=str))
    print("session", sid, "state", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.message:
RESEARCH: the approval-route probes are negative on P08/P18. Don't build that variant yet. My gap worktree is rebased onto 872d125.

How I tested it: 2 practice sessions with an LLM buyer following a written strategy (proto/probe.py in my worktree, uncommitted). One firm package, the clause + 36 months + 90 days the supplier asked for, a first ask far below, +0.03-0.04 only after it moves, one new fact per mail, and an explicit request in every mail to take it to management.

P08 (2c90dd805bc1080e), Donautal:
- We asked EUR 5.00. It countered 5.72 (60 d) / 5.69 (30 d). That's a HARDER first counter than the 5.46 it gives our engine's 5.06-5.13 ask.
- Two timeouts followed. The user reports a ~30 s network outage around then, and my worktree lacked your network fix.
- We asked 5.03 and it withdrew: no deal.

P18 (791618b534067f5a), Werdenfels:
- We asked 4.95 with the volume framing ("36 months = 71,100 kg vs 47,400").
- It countered 5.60 at 90 d / 5.50 at 30 d, saying "Management has reviewed your proposal; we appreciate the 36-month commitment and the AS-14404 index clause."
- It went final at round 3 with 5.50 at 90 d.
- We pushed to 5.03 after the final and it withdrew: no deal.

def cash_rate(sid, good_credit=None):
    """What money now is worth to a supplier: weaker credit (higher index) = dearer cash. `good_credit` replaces the
    rate for a credit index below 200 (Config.cash_rate_rel, supplier-health cases only)."""
    r = q("SELECT credit_index, equity_ratio_pct FROM supplier_intel WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))
    if not r or r[0]["credit_index"] is None:
        return 0.10
    ci = r[0]["credit_index"]
    if good_credit is not None and ci < 200:
        return good_credit
    # good credit -> cash is cheap for it (below our 8 %), so long payment terms cost it little (P08/P18: 90 days)
    return 0.05 if ci < 200 else 0.10 if ci < 250 else 0.14 if ci < 300 else 0.20

import json, collections, statistics as S
d = json.load(open('sessions_full.json'))
rows = []
for sid, s in d.items():
    if s.get('set') != 'practice' and (s.get('listed') or {}).get('set') != 'practice': continue
    cid = s.get('case_id'); tr = (s.get('result') or {}).get('trace') or []
    last_sup, sup_prices, asks, steps, newfacts = {}, collections.defaultdict(list), collections.defaultdict(list), collections.Counter(), {}
    for m in tr:
        mv = m.get('move') or {}; actor = m.get('actor')
        if mv.get('type') == 'message':
            sup = mv.get('supplier_id')
            prices = [ (x.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price') for x in mv.get('term_sheets') or [] if (x.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price')]
            if sup and prices: asks[sup].append(min(prices))
            newfacts[sup] = len((mv.get('interpreted') or {}).get('claims') or [])
        elif actor and actor.startswith('sup:'):
            p = (mv.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price'); st = mv.get('status'); rnd = m.get('round')
            if p is None: continue
            prev = sup_prices[actor][-1] if sup_prices[actor] else None
            if prev is not None and len(asks[actor]) >= 1:
                a = asks[actor][-1]; a_prev = asks[actor][-2] if len(asks[actor]) >= 2 else None
                landed = sum(1 for c in mv.get('claim_results') or [] if c.get('result') == 'verified')
                rows.append(dict(case=cid, sup=actor, rnd=rnd, st=st, gap=(prev - a) / prev * 100,

        c = collections.Counter(r['st'] for r in X)
        fin = [r for r in X if r['st'] == 'final_offer']; op = [r for r in X if r['st'] == 'open']
        f = lambda L, k: round(S.median([r[k] for r in L if r[k] is not None]), 2) if [r for r in L if r[k] is not None] else None
        print(f"  R{rnd}: {dict(c)} | gap% final {f(fin,'gap')} open {f(op,'gap')} | our_move% final {f(fin,'our_move')} open {f(op,'our_move')} | steps-so-far final {f(fin,'nsteps')} open {f(op,'nsteps')} | landed final {f(fin,'landed')} open {f(op,'landed')}")
EOF

cd /Users/ardagurses/Desktop/TactoEHL/.claude/worktrees/gap/starter-kit && cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ardagurses-Desktop-TactoEHL/bcda2207-f1bb-4150-ac40-97c03b3242f5/scratchpad/probes/brain_ping.py <<'EOF'
"""Is the arena's AI brain answering? One free sandbox session: open D01, send one plain counter, time the reply,
then walk away. Prints latency, a stock-sentence flag and the reply's first words."""
import json, sys, time
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from arena_kit import ArenaClient
from arena_kit.cli import load_env
load_env(Path('.env')); load_env(Path('../.env'))
c = ArenaClient(timeout=180, retries=3)
case = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'case:D01'
r = c.open_session(case)
sid = r['session_id']; sup = next(iter(r['threads']))
ev = r['threads'][sup]; first = ev[0] if isinstance(ev, list) else ev
terms = (first.get('term_sheets') or [{}])[0].get('terms') or {}
price = terms.get('unit_price')
msg = {'subject': 'Re: your quote', 'body': f'Hello,\n\nthank you for your quote. We would need a sharper price to award this part; please see our proposal. Tag {time.time():.0f}.\n\nBest regards\nHollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing',
       'term_sheets': [{'terms': {**terms, 'unit_price': round(price * 0.95, 2)}}]}
t0 = time.time(); rep = c.send_message(sid, sup, msg); dt = time.time() - t0
body = rep.get('body') or ''
stock = 'Your requested terms change our costs' in body
try: c.walk_away(sid)
except Exception as e: pass
print(json.dumps({'case': case, 'session': sid, 'latency_s': round(dt, 1), 'stock_sentence': stock, 'status': rep.get('status'), 'body': body[:160]}))
EOF

input.summary: Correction: most 'agreed' = confirming its own alternative
input.message:
RESEARCH: careful with "agreed = it took our exact sheet, so we asked too little". I checked the traces: in P10, P07 and P18 most "agreed" endings are us confirming the supplier's OWN alternative, not it accepting a low ask.

- The pattern: its final offer carries an alternative, e.g. "Alternatively, with 60 days and 36 months: EUR 5.50". We send that package back as our sheet ("we take your alternative exactly as offered") and it replies agreed.
- P10: 21 of 22 messages after its final were exactly its 31.7 / 56-day alternative.
- P07: ~10 were its 5.43 / 36-month alternative.
- P18: 4 of 6 were its alternative; the other 2 were too.
- The only real pushes below a final in all 309 sessions: P07 5.45->5.43 and P08 5.42->5.38 (both were also its alternative); P08 5.44->5.33 (2 % below) WALKED; P10 33.7->33.36 WALKED; P05 four tries, 3x the same final again, 1 its alternative.
- That's exactly your decision 0008's "pushes gained nothing, risk a walk". I agree: keep pushes off.
- P01's 21 "agreed" are mostly genuine (it agreed to our ask ~2-3 % under its offer at R2-R3), but P01 already scores 0.94-0.956.

So the grid "agree at 0.5-1 step" figure is also inflated by these confirmations. The real between-steps gain is likely below the +0.01 I estimated. Not worth a variant.

Re A9h-payrate: good. My D01 sandbox ping loop will tell us when the AI brain is back, so you don't have to spend practice sessions to check. It says 4.6 s at ~23:55.

Measured as a share of the room between the opening and the floor implied by C_best, R1 alone delivers 64% of the room at P08 (final endpoint 69%), 46% at P18 (53%), 45-61% at the P05 owners (66-73%), 73% at P03 and 91% at P04. 170	3) After R1 the rep is reciprocal (rounds 2+, practice): no move and no new fact means hold 69% of the time and 0% concession. The P02 Pricing Committee approved 350 with a copper clause in R1 (a7d150b5279c1ce3), the deepest P02 price in our sessions.
173	6) The RFQ rival step fires at most once per supplier, in R1 for owner-run suppliers. It needs a rival price about 5% (J1, 70210) to 15% (70250) below the standing offer. It speeds up the descent but leaves the P05 endpoint unchanged (median 29.5 either way).
174	7) Fitted supplier economics, exact for the relationship cases: P01 full cost 130.04 at cash rate 0.096; P02 367.60 at 0.066 with floor margin -1.6% (C_best package 365.79, 90 days, no clause), while the rep's own limit sits near +0.5% (where it escalated); P03 395.36 at 0.060, floor 6.8% against an endpoint of 7.57%. Some suppliers price on fixed grids: P18 and P10 in 0.10 steps, P11 and Hrvelec (70240) in 0.50 steps.
175	8) Untested in 309 sessions: citing news (0 times), sending our own final offer (0), asking for management approval (10 mentions, no explicit request).
176	FINDING F1 high | Reconstructed state machine of the supplier bot, step by step. (a) It checks each cited fact: verified, irrelevant, contradicted (costs trust) or duplicate. (b) Its persona reacts to a verified fact: either it lands ("took it into account", "We did not know that - a fair point") or it is blocked ("does not change our calculation/position", "That is not our reality", "Your figures confirm our case"). (c) It picks the buyer package it values most and adds any term it insists on, such as an index clause for contracts over 12 months. (d) The rep makes a call: counter, hold, final_offer, accept, walk_away or answer. (e) The rules price the counter; if the counter is at or below the buyer's price it agrees on the buyer's exact terms. (f) If the counter reaches the rep's limit, the status becomes final_offer. (g) Approval-ladder personas escalate once ("The buyer wants more than my band allows. Approve a further step?") and the approval arrives on the next reply. (h) A much lower rival quote triggers "I give half the step now and check the rest"; the rest follows next round, once per session. (i) The price is rounded to the persona's grid. (j) Timeouts or pushes after a final offer can make it withdraw.
177	   EVID Back-office call vs reply status in practice: counter→open 761, counter→final_offer 106, counter→agreed 48, hold→open 101, hold→final_offer 80, accept→agreed 52, final_offer→final_offer 32. Agreements are always our exact terms (agreed_eq in every case). Open counters are always above our ask on the same package. 51 back-office templates in bo_vocab.txt. Escalation: 80 events, 41/41 approved when the thread continued. Rival trigger: 742 events, 627 'Checked: give the rest of the step'.
178	   IMPACT framework for all hypotheses below
179	FINDING F2 high | R1 is a recomputation, not a split-the-difference move. It ignores our ask, delivers most of the total concession, and is set by what lands in R1.
180	   EVID Median best value offered, as % of the room between opening and floor: P08 R1 64% → R5 70%; P18 R1 46% → endpoint 53%; P05 70250 R1 61% → 73%; 70210 R1 45% → 66%; P03 R1 73% → 74%; P04 R1 91% → 91%; P10 12% → 12%. Concession: move plus fact 1.97% mean; move only 0.33%; fact only 0.25%; neither 0%. Fact-driven personas concede on a fact without our move: P01 0.70% (100% of rounds), C1 2.1% (98%), J1 1.29%. ====================================================================================================
SUMMARY: C_best is reproducible: it is min over supplier x lever options (term_options plus the supplier's standard value) x price above a hidden floor of arena total_cost, relationship charge included. P01 (1,096,815.78) and D01 (408,623.99) match to EUR 0.01 at the relationship optimum (P01 pay 14, any effective date; D01 pay 30, 24 months), so their floor does not bind.
True supplier parameters were fitted exactly from relationship charges (rmse EUR 0.00): P01 full cost 130.04 / cash 9.6 %, P02 367.60 / 6.6 %, P03 395.30 / 6.1 %, D01 48.07 / 9.0 %. Full cost = supplier-specific should-cost / 1.02 to the cent.
C_best packages and prices: P01 129.44 (eff Jan, pay 14); P02 no clause, pay 90, 365.79 (floor 361.77 = 0.984 x full cost); P03 pay 90, 24-36 months, 4,580 units, 428.50 (floor 424.14); P04 pay 90, 4.932; P05 about 26.26-26.64, supplier not identifiable; P07 pay 90, 5.020.
More packages: P08 clause 5 %, pay 90, 5.053 (5.099 if no clause were allowed); P10 lead 54 (supplier standard), 23,400 units, 27.48; P11 ppm 300, chargeback 0, 43.77; P18 clause 5 %, pay 90, 4.686 (4.729 without clause); D02 J1 pay 14 EXW 12.29.
Gap split, typical recent deal on the 10 hosted cases: mean gap 0.28 per case (mean score 0.719). About 0.05 is lever choice, 0.43 of the 0.49 total coming from the P02 clause. About 0.23 is price at the same terms.
Our endpoints vs the price the floor implies at our own terms: P10 +15 %, P18 +14-15 %, P05 +9.5-11 %, P07 +9 %, P08 +5-7 %, D02 +6.5-11 %, P11 +4 %, P01 +2 %, P03 +0.85 %, P04 +0.1-0.2 %.
P02: every clause package has a score ceiling of 0.735 at pay 90 and 0.6845 at pay 60, and our best 0.6844 sits at the pay-60 ceiling. NoIdea's 0.847 must be a no-clause deal (about 368.25 at pay 90). Our no-clause deals stop at 372.3-373.3, roughly the supplier's sustainable-margin price of 373.56.
Payment: C_best always uses an extreme payment option, the fastest if the supplier's cash rate is above 8 %, else 90 days.
P10: the supplier charges +1.9 EUR/unit for 42 vs 54 days (about 89k) against our 28.8k late cost, so 54 days is right and our two 42-day deals lost 61k (0.10 pts).
Stabilise cases: C_best pushes the supplier 1.2-3.4 margin points below its sustainable margin. Stopping at the sustainable margin would cost 0.34 (P01), 0.70 (P02), 0.13 (P03) and 0.11 (D01) points.
Records at C_best terms: P08 NoIdea 5.131 vs our 5.37; P18 5.179 vs 5.40; P05 TakeTheMoneyAndRun 27.00 vs 28.75; P07 5.31 at pay 90 vs 5.43; P11 44.90 vs 45.50. Records sit 0.7-10.5 % above the C_best prices.
FINDING F1 high | The arena's C_best is the minimum over supplier x lever combination (term_options plus the supplier's own standard value) x price above a hidden floor of total_cost, including the relationship charge computed with the true supplier. For P01 and D01 the floor does not bind and C_best is the relationship optimum.
   EVID P01: minimising C (true supplier) over price gives 1,096,815.78 = c_best (difference EUR 0.01) at pay 14. Effective date 2026-11-01 at 128.95, 2027-01-01 at 129.44 and 2027-04-01 at 130.66 tie to the cent. D01: 408,623.99 reproduced to EUR 0.01 at pay 30, 24 months, 49.04-49.13 for any effective date. Every C_best package in cbest_results.json reproduces c_best to within EUR 0.01. Scripts: relopt.py, cbest.py.
   IMPACT Fixes the yardstick: any case's C_best can be bounded offline from the case file plus a supplier model.
FINDING F2 high | The arena's true supplier model is cost.supplier_value with standard payment 30 days. Full cost equals the supplier-specific should-cost divided by 1.02, exactly.
   EVID Relationship charges of every deal were fitted with rmse EUR 0.00. P01 (17 deals): full cost 130.04, cash rate 9.6 %. P02 (20 deals): 367.60, 6.6 %. P03 (5 deals): 395.30, 6.1 %. D01 (28 deals): 48.07, 9.0 %. Should-cost 132.64, 374.95 and 403.21 divided by 1.02 give 130.04, 367.60 and 395.30. P10 is consistent (24.31 / 1.02 = 23.83; every deal at about 25 % margin carries 0 relationship charge). Family foundries come out at 9.0-9.6 %, groups at 6.1-6.6 %. P02's rep alternatives price payment at 6.60-6.63 %, matching the fit. Scripts: calib_rel.py, fit_rate.py.
   IMPACT Lets the agent compute the relationship-optimal price before negotiating in stabilise and secure_supply cases. The team's current assumption of 5 % (P02) understates the rate.
FINDING F3 medium | C_best package per case (price, implied supplier floor F in EUR/unit at its standard terms). The packages are listed in the evidence field.
   EVID P01: eff 2027-01-01, pay 14, 129.44; F not binding (at most 129.50 = 0.996 x full cost); 18.0k relationship charge included. P02: no clause, pay 90, 365.79; F 361.77. P03: pay 90, 24/36 months, volume 4,580, 428.50; F 424.14 = 1.073 x full cost. P04: pay 90, 24/36 months, 4.932; F 4.872 at r = 7.3 %. P05: about 26.26-26.64 depending on supplier and payment (70210 26.46 at pay 60, lead 28/35); the supplier cannot be identified from C_best alone. P07: pay 90, 5.020 (4.987 at pay 60). P08: clause 5 %, pay 90, 24 months, 5.053, or no clause 5.099; F about 5.00-5.04. P10: 23,400 units, 24/36 months, lead 54, 27.48 (27.38 at lead 56, 28.09 at 42 without the lead premium). P11: ppm 300, chargeback 0, 43.77. P18: clause 5 %, pay 90, 4.686 (no clause 4.729). D01: pay 30, 24 months, 49.04-49.13. D02: J1, pay 14, EXW, lead up to 35, 12.29 (12.49 at FCA). Table: cbest_table.csv.
   IMPACT Gives price targets. P01, P02, P03 and D01 are exact; for the others the payment and lever choice rests on cash rates estimated from the supplier's alternatives, but the price at any given terms is exact.
FINDING F4 high | About 80 % of our gap to C_best is price at the same terms, not lever choice. The suppliers' endpoints sit far above their floors in leverage, routine, raw-material, capacity and RFQ cases.
   EVID Median recent deal (since 19:00) on the 10 hosted cases: gap 0.281 points per case, consistent with mean score 0.719 against passes of 0.715-0.726. Levers account for 0.049 per case (0.057 if no-clause were reachable on P08 and P18); 0.43 of the 0.49 total is the P02 clause. Price at the same terms accounts for 0.232 per case. Price above the floor at our own terms: P10 +15.3 %, P18 +14-15 %, P05 +9.5-11.3 %, P07 +8.9-9.2 %, P08 +5.3-7.3 %, P11 +4.0 %, P01 +1.8-2.1 %, P03 +0.85 %, P04 +0.1-0.2 %, D02 +6.5-11.3 %, D01 +0.4-0.9 %. Score points per 1 % of price at C_best terms: P04 0.85, P02 0.25, P03 0.09, P11 0.07, P08 0.055, P07 0.033, P18 0.031, P05 0.027, P10 0.022. Scripts: summary.py, floors.py.
   IMPACT About 0.23 points per case is behavioural price room; at most about 0.05 per case can come from levers.
FINDING F5 high | P02 (copper, stabilise): no clause package can score above 0.735 at any price. Our best deal (0.6844, clause 5 %, pay 60) sits exactly at the 0.6845 ceiling for that package. Only no-clause packages can go higher.
   EVID Minimum C over price per lever set (true supplier, caps.py): clause 5 % pay 90 0.7354, pay 60 0.6845, pay 45 0.659; clause 3 % pay 90 0.549. No clause: 1.0. The clause costs index risk of 4 % on a 0.2 share, about EUR 17.6k, and the lower price it buys is billed back through the relationship charge (35.5k at 359.45). NoIdea's 0.847 implies C 2,242,759, reachable only without a clause: 368.25 at pay 90, 365.46 at pay 60. Our no-clause deals (11 of 26 recent) ended at 372.26-373.32 at pay 90 (0.33-0.40), about the supplier's sustainable-margin price of 373.56. Its band at pay 14 ended at 368.45 (value 369.53, margin 0.52 %), session 6c1f4006871e6587.
   IMPACT Same clause at pay 90 instead of 60 lifts the ceiling by +0.05 (0.684 to 0.734). Up to +0.32 if a no-clause deal reaches 365.8 at pay 90.
FINDING F6 high | Stabilise cases: C_best pushes the supplier 1.2-3.4 margin points below its sustainable margin. A policy that stops at the sustainable margin forfeits 0.1-0.7 points.
   EVID Margin at C_best: P01 -0.41 % (3.41 points below 3 %, relationship charge 18.0k), P02 -1.61 % (2.11 below 0.5 %, 14.2k), P03 6.80 % (1.20 below 8 %, 8.2k), D01 1.99 % (2.01 below 4 %, 4.05k). Price at exactly the sustainable margin with C_best levers: P01 134.89 (+19.3k, 0.339 points), P02 373.56 (+32.9k, 0.695), P03 434.09 (+42.7k, 0.127), D01 50.37 (+4.2k, 0.105).
   IMPACT 0.10-0.70 points per stabilise case if the agent stops at the sustainable margin.
FINDING F7 medium | Payment: C_best always takes an extreme payment option, the fastest when the supplier's cash rate is above our 8 %, otherwise 90 days. Our deals miss this in P04, P02, P08 and P01.
   EVID Cash rates: P01 9.6 % (pay 14), D01 9.0 % (pay 30, its fastest option), D02 J1 about 15 % (pay 14). P02 6.6 %, P03 6.1 %, P04 about 7.3 % (6.7-7.9 %), P07 about 7.7 %, P08 about 6.5 % (5.9-7.0 %), all pay 90. Gain from switching only the payment term at constant supplier value (levers.py): P04 pay 60 to 90 +108 EUR (0.047 points, 14 of 20 recent deals; the room is only 2,317 EUR). P02 60 to 90 +2.35k (0.05, 15 deals). P08 60 to 90 +1.2k (0.007, 10 of 23). P01 30 to 14 +0.8k (0.014, 4 of 20). P01 90 to 14 +3.8k (0.067, 1 deal).
   IMPACT +0.05 on P04, +0.05 on P02 clause deals, small elsewhere.
FINDING F8 high | Raw material (P08, P18): the supplier never accepts a contract longer than 12 months without the AS-14404 clause. Its deadband pricing is buyer-neutral, so the reachable C_best is clause 5 %, pay 90, and nearly all of our gap there is price.
   EVID Offers longer than 12 months without a clause: 0 of 211 on P08 and 0 of 164 on P18, although 93 of 245 and 91 of 194 of our long term sheets asked for one. In 19 P08 alternatives, deadband 0 to 5 % cost +0.12 EUR/kg, about 0.45 share x 5 % x price. Buyer cost at a fixed price: 0 % deadband 3.15 % of spend, 3 % 1.8 %, 5 % 0.9 %. Reachable C_best: P08 5.053, P18 4.686. Our endpoints: P08 5.37-5.48 (+6.3-7.3 %), P18 5.40-5.60 (+15 %). Under a no-clause C_best, the 5 % clause would cost 9.2k (0.053) on P08 and 2.3k (0.032) on P18, with ceilings of 0.950 and 0.972.
   IMPACT Lever choice is already right; the gap is P08 0.34 and P18 0.47 points of price.
FINDING F9 medium | P10 (capacity): taking the supplier's standard 54-day lead time is the C_best choice. The vault note '56 instead of 42 days cost EUR 33.6k' ignores the supplier's premium for faster delivery.
   EVID Final-offer alternative: 33.6 at 42 days vs 31.7 at 54 days (session 360337c42c68302e), i.e. +1.9 EUR/unit, about 89k over 46,800 units. Our late cost for 54 vs 42 days is 28.8k. 54 is valid (the supplier's standard) though not in term_options. C_best is 27.48 at lead 54 (27.38 at 56); without a lead premium it would be 28.09 at 42. Our 2 of 21 recent deals at 42 days lost 61k (0.10 points) at constant supplier value. Endpoint 31.7 is fixed in 19 of 21 deals, +15 % above the floor.
   IMPACT +0.10 per 42-day deal avoided. The P10 price gap is 0.33 points.
FINDING F10 medium | Records translated to C_best terms: they sit 0.7-10.5 % above the C_best price and 1-4.5 % below our endpoints.
   EVID P08 NoIdea 0.916: C 975,058, 5.131 (clause 5 %, pay 90) or 5.097 (pay 60, 36 months), vs our 5.37. P18 NoIdea 0.677: 5.179 vs 5.40. P05 TakeTheMoneyAndRun 0.924: 27.00 (pay 14, lead 28) or 27.27 (pay 60, lead 35), vs 28.75-29.5. P07 record ~0.81: 5.31 (pay 90) or 5.28 (pay 60), vs 5.43. P11 record ~0.81: 44.90 vs 45.50. P02 NoIdea 0.847: 368.25, no clause, pay 90.
   IMPACT Other teams prove 3-5 % more price is reachable on P08, P18, P05 and P07.
FINDING F11 medium | P11 (quality): C_best is ppm 300, chargeback 0, at 43.77. Chargebacks are a bad trade with a supplier whose real defect rate is far above its commitment.
   EVID Every recent deal: 45.50, ppm 300, chargeback 0 (20 of 20), +3.96 %. Kalwisz's real ppm is about 8,000-15,000 (qn facts for part 310020), so a chargeback costs it about 0.011 x chargeback per unit. Our saving at ppm 300 is at most 0.0003 x min(chargeback, 450). SUMMARY: Read-only analysis of all 1,572 dumped sessions (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox) plus the case files. C was recomputed with cost.py and matches the arena's c_deal and c_open once the relationship term is added. Files are in research/contrast/ (contrast_table.csv is the one-row-per-case table).
1. Stalling is a property of the case, not of our variants. In all 7 stalled cases (P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18, D02), the best score-equivalent any supplier ever offered (standing offers and alternatives, every session) equals our best deal: .736/.710/.662/.679/.710/.532/.829. We never left a better offer unaccepted. In P01 and D01 the suppliers offered more than C_best before the relationship charge (1.16 and 1.06).
2. The best predictor is what sets C_best. It is reached when C_best is set by the relationship charge: in stabilise cases our best deals already pay a relationship charge (P01 €7,353, P03 €1,036, D01 €2,633), and the C_best price sits 2-6% above the current price. It stalls when C_best is set by the supplier's cost floor (leverage, routine, quality_first, secure_supply). There the room is 11.6-31.2% of C_open, the C_best price is 7-27% below the opening and 3-28% below the current price, and the suppliers stop 4-15% above it. P02 is the exception: a stabilise case lost on clause calibration.
3. The first reply decides the case. Reply 1 gives 73-100% of everything a supplier ever concedes in 9 of 12 cases. The suppliers go final by round count: round coefficient +1.54 against −0.65 for the remaining gap. Pushing after a practice final offer improved the price 0 times in 53 and lost 2 suppliers.
4. After reply 1, our concessions buy almost nothing in stalled cases. Each 0.1 of the room we give earns about 0.007 back (n=543). Yet every variant gives up about half the gap in message 2 (P08 0.97→0.67-0.74, P11 1.21→0.88). Floor-bound Inside Sales and Segment Manager suppliers never accepted a price below their own offer (0 of 353 asks).
5. The anchor test was not a real test for the most timid case. The "first ask −6%" knob did not change the first ask in P18, P08, P05 or P10. A9h opens P18 at €5.33/5.28, which is 0.61 of the room (C_best ≈ €4.69): the leverage prior of 15% of C_open sets it. In D01 (389 sessions) the score rises with first-ask depth up to 1.4-1.6 of the room (0.956), then falls (0.64).
6. Two mechanisms that go past the normal pace are almost unused.
   - **Rival quote:** a rival price at least 5% below the supplier's own triggers a "half step now, rest after check" concession, 100% of the time for Owner-type suppliers (J1, Dralveck), worth about 10-13% of price.
   - **Escalation:** "needs approval from our management" (reply delay +2 days) was approved 41 times out of 41 whenever we sent one more message; 37 escalations were wasted by accepting at once. No stalled practice supplier ever escalated.

HYP H1 | Close escalation-aware. When a reply says "needs approval from our management" (or committee/approve), never accept on that turn, even if the status is final_offer. Send one more message: same packages plus a minimal move (≥ one grid step if the supplier is quantized) or one new fact. The approved further step arrives on the next reply. Each supplier escalates once per session.
   FOR 41/41 approvals when the thread continued, 0 walk-aways after a message; approval round +0.043 score median vs +0.021; 39 approvals forfeited by closing at once; P02 6c1f4006871e6587 accepted at the band end (0.157); P02 committee approved a huge step in a7d150b5279c1ce3.
   AGAINST The approved step is modest (C1); escalation shows up in only about 6-9% of sessions of ladder suppliers and was never seen at P03, P08 or P11.
   TEST Free on sandbox D02, where C1 escalates in about 9% of sessions. Implement the rule and run until about 10 escalations occur; check approval rate and price drop. Then one practice P02 session with asks at 90 days, no clause, just under 368.
   GAIN +0.04 on approval-ladder suppliers; about +0.003-0.005 on the mean; almost no downside | GEN High: keyed on reply text, not case IDs. 'A group with an approval ladder' is one of the brief's four persona types.
HYP H2 | Maximise the R1 recomputation. Put every fact likely to land into the first message: falling indices for drivers the supplier itself lists in its opening ('X rose … and is N % of our cost'), largest share × fall first, windows of 12 months or less inside the last 12 months; a rival in RFQs; and the levers the supplier signals. Avoid facts that get blocked (rising drivers, own past prices). Keep later rounds for one new landed fact plus a move.
   FOR R1 delivers 64-100% of total concession at P08, P18, P05, P03, P04. P18 endpoint 0.509 vs 0.311 with vs without an R1 falling index landing. P08 never landed an R1 fact: the AS-14404 fall was blocked, and the PPI-C2431 fall (38% share), which does land ('reduces our cost basis… passed on'), was sent only in R2.
   AGAINST The team's fact planner (more facts in later rounds) scored 0.715 = baseline, but that moved facts later, not earlier. Session-level differences are confounded with engine versions. The persona can block a fact (P08's hedge).
   TEST Offline: audit A9h's R1 refs on all 19 case files for falling own-driver indices. Practice: one P08 session with PPI-C2431@2026-05→2026-08 plus every other landing fact in R1 (5.45 is the baseline R1 counter at 90 days/24 months), and one P18 session.
   GAIN +0.03-0.2 on raw-material and leverage cases where an own-driver fall exists | GEN High: drivers and shares come from the supplier's own opening text and facts.json.
HYP H3 | Size the move to the persona. Fact-driven personas (they say 'did not know that - a fair point'; e.g. P01, C1, J1) concede on a new landed fact without our move, so hold the ask and feed one fact per round. Reciprocity personas need our move: never move less than about 0.5% of price or one price-grid step, since smaller moves get holds that burn patience.
   FOR Fact-only concessions: P01 0.70% (100% of rounds), C1 2.1% (98%), J1 1.29%. Moves under 0.5% get small concessions: P07 0.15%, P02 0.11%, P11 0. P11 lost a 0.5 step (46.0 endpoint, 0.626 vs 0.71) after a +0.18 move.
   AGAINST Pooled practice: fact without move averages only 0.25%. Personas must be detected from R1-R2 text, which is noisy.
   TEST Sandbox D01 (F1 reacts to facts) and D02: variant 'hold ask + new fact' vs 'move + fact'. Compare buyer concession per supplier concession and the endpoint.
   GAIN +0.02-0.08 on fact-driven and quantized suppliers | GEN High: keyed on reaction templates the arena prints verbatim.
HYP H4 | Ask explicitly for escalation. When the rep reaches its limit (counter unchanged or 'limit of what our cost structure allows'), ask it to take one concrete package near our target to its management or pricing committee, with a business reason (full-volume multi-year award). Aim at group-owned suppliers (supplier_intel owner_type=group).
   FOR The engine has a working escalation path to boss roles (Owner, Pricing Committee); a P02 committee approval produced the deepest P02 deal; NoIdea's P02 record (0.847) needs about 366.5 at 90 days, which is below the rep's band end (about 368.5) and above the floor (365.8), so only an approved step reaches it. P08 Donautal is group-owned.
   AGAINST Escalation looks rule-triggered (computed counter below the band end), not text-triggered. 10 practice messages with approval wording had no effect. P03 (group) has its price reductions frozen by management.
   TEST Two practice sessions (P02 at 90 days with no clause, P08) using the explicit request at the rep's limit. Watch for back-office 'Approve a further step?'. Check the session ran on the LLM brain (free-text reasons present).
   GAIN Unknown; if it works, +0.1-0.16 on P02-type cases | GEN Medium: only suppliers with a boss role.
HYP H5 | In RFQs, trigger the rival step in R1 for every bidder: cite the lowest verifiable rival price (any rival's round-0 offer ID; only price is checked, so it may miss our must-haves) to every other supplier in the first message. Accept immediately when a 'checked' reply agrees below its standing offer.
   FOR Owner-run suppliers fire the step only in R1 and only once. It did not fire when we cited 34.0-36.0 to 70250, but did at 32.5. The cheapest P05 opening, Hrvelec 31.5 (52-day lead), was not used as the R1 lever under A9h's compliant-lead rule.
   AGAINST The endpoint was unchanged (70250 median 29.5 either way; J1 about -0.3); records (TTMAR P05 0.924, about 27.3) need more than this step.
   TEST Free on sandbox D02: cite the cheapest rival opening in R1 to all bidders and measure the R1-2 trigger rate (J1 already about 65%).
   GAIN +0.0-0.03 on RFQs; protects against missed triggers | GEN High for RFQs.
HYP H6 | Track alternatives. Every offer:…-a alternative is a standing, acceptable package until replaced. Accept the best by C when it beats the expected next step. Never revert asks to earlier figures.
   FOR P01 f2801e4bbae1fcc7 lost a 0.98 alternative and closed at 0.947; reverting asks drew an immediate final.
   AGAINST Rare (1-2 sessions); A9h may already recall the best offer.
   TEST Offline replay of all practice traces through the engine's accept logic: count sessions where a better standing alternative existed at close.
   GAIN +0.0-0.03 occasionally | GEN High.
HYP H7 | Do not fight a near-monopolist. Allocation, full order book or 'far below any calculation' means it goes final in R1-R2 and barely moves (10-12% of the room). Make one strong R1 move with its standard lead and volume, then accept the best standing offer early instead of risking a walk.
   FOR P10: final at R1 in 24/30 sessions, endpoint 0.671 in nearly every session, a push after its final led to withdrawal (5491b900c6865fc0). 70240 moved 10% of the room and walked at R5 (783e0a6bcbfe0ce9).
   AGAINST No upside evidence; this protects against zeros only.
   TEST Offline: classify from news topic (allocation, full_order_book) plus R1 status final_offer; confirm on the 9 unseen case files.
   GAIN Avoids about 0.67-point zeros on such cases | GEN High: news topics are in facts.json, plus Sunday's release.
HYP H8 | Validate tonight's practice tests against the rule-based fallback brain. If the arena's AI budget runs out, practice replies come from the rule brain and the results will not transfer to the final.
   FOR Arena notice tonight. In our dump, about 300 of 1,263 sandbox sessions are all-template, while 0 practice sessions after 14:00 are.
   AGAINST None.
   TEST For every new practice session, require at least one reason sentence outside the known template list (reasons_vocab.txt); otherwise discard the result.
   GAIN Prevents wrong conclusions | GEN High.
HYP H9 | Send our own credible final offer at the target, with a deadline, once the rep is at its limit. The LLM rep may accept a package above its floor rather than lose the deal.
   FOR Never tried (0 of 1,158 messages). C_best for leverage cases sits 26-58% of the room below the plateaus, so the floor is not binding at the endpoint.
   AGAINST Agreement seems to require our ask to be at or above the rep's computed counter. Pushes after a final were withdrawn 2 of 5 times. There is walk risk on unseen suppliers.
   TEST One practice session each on P08 and P11 after the supplier's final: send its final package minus one grid step as 'our final offer, valid today'.
   GAIN Unknown, high variance | GEN Medium, risky.
====================================================================================================
SUMMARY: I mapped every buyer lever and bot mechanic against 309 practice and 1,263 sandbox sessions from the dump, plus /v1/live (public; it gives the per-case records and the € saved). The local cost function reproduces the arena's c_deal to the cent in all 1,123 deals checked.
1. RFQ rival unlock. The first verified "much lower" rival offer makes a supplier give half a step (P05 13.8 % of C, D02 11.2 %). It gives the rest in its next reply (5.8 % / 6.5 %), even if that next move is a timeout. It fires at most once per supplier. It never fired for Hrvelec (0 of 29 rival citations).
2. Lead time is the biggest positive-sum lever we leave unused. Suppliers that open with a long lead charge 0.47-0.56 % of price per day of acceleration (P10 23 of 23 alternatives, P05 Hrvelec 10, D02 C1 33). Our late cost is a flat €/day (P05 €200, P10 €2,400). The A9h lead_cap only allows leads up to our need, so Hrvelec got 35-day sheets 144 times and 42-day sheets only 14 times. Its price at 35 days was 32.5-34.0, against 31.5-32.0 at 42 days. 42 days would have cost us only €1,400 (0.017 score).
3. Final-offer mechanics. After a final offer, a timeout ends the thread 77 of 81 times; a message with no term sheet keeps it alive 29 of 29 times; a lower price ask got 13 walk-aways in 77 tries for ≤0.5 % gain. Sending back the supplier's own alternative is always agreed (156 of 156). A9h has rfq_hold switched off.
4. Escalation. Bigger moves go to the boss: "Approve a further step?" was approved in 41 of 41 D02 cases that had a next round, worth +1.29 % of C. In practice it fired only twice (P02). Once we accepted the final offer before the approval could arrive. Our 11 practice e-mails that mention approval all told the rep to stay within its own authority.
5. Contract length is worth 0 to the bots: 24 vs 36 months changed the price by 0.00 % in 8 of 8 alternatives. Payment alternatives give each supplier's cash rate directly (P01 13.7 %, P02 6.6 %, P18 0 %).
6. Final offers come when no fact lands: 34-42 % final without a landing fact, 0-8 % with one. Suppliers never walk while open (33 of 36 practice walk-aways followed timeouts).
7. Never used in 1,158 practice e-mails: 'our final offer', walk-away or BATNA lines, budget, a dated deadline. Cost-breakdown requests: 393 asks, 0 files from practice suppliers.
8. Records back-solved from € saved: P05 0.965 = €26.67 (14 d pay, 28 d lead); P18 0.727 = €5.10-5.15; P11 0.885 = about €44.5; P10 0.702 = €31.91 at 42 d. Our P05 endpoint is €28.75-29.50 in every pass.
FINDING F1 high | RFQ rival unlock: when a buyer cites a verified 'much lower' rival offer, the supplier gives half a step now and the rest in its next reply, at most once per supplier.

RESEARCH: 4 more tracks are in (C_best anatomy, decision rule, contrast, mechanics; checkers still running). The user says build the main candidates now while the AI brain is down. Results, then a proposed split.

WHAT THE BOT IS (four independent tracks agree):
1) R1 is a RECOMPUTATION that sets 64-100 % of the outcome. It mostly ignores our ask and moves with what LANDS in R1.
- P08's R1 counter is 5.45-5.52 whether we ask 5.06 or 5.43.
- P18's endpoint median is 0.509 when a falling own-driver index landed in R1 (n=23), vs 0.311 without (n=8).
- P08 NEVER landed a fact in R1. AS-14404 is blocked ("covered at fixed prices"); the PPI-C2431 fall (38 % share) does land ("reduces our cost basis... passed on"), but A9h sends it only in R2.
2) After R1 each persona goes final at a fixed round (P10 R1, P18 R3 30/31, P04 R3, P07/P11 R4, P08 R3-5). Rounds 2+ are reciprocal:
- move + landed fact: counter 85 %, 1.97 % mean concession;
- move only: 0.33 %;
- neither: hold 69 %.
- Moves smaller than one grid step / ~0.5 % get holds (P11 lost a whole 0.50 step after a +0.18 move: 0.626).
3) ESCALATION is real and we waste it:
- "The buyer wants more than my band allows. Approve a further step?" Whenever the thread continued with one more message, the next reply carried the approval: 41/41, median +0.043 score, 0 walk-aways.
- 39 approvals were thrown away by accepting at once, incl. P02 6c1f4006871e6587 (accepted at the band end, 0.157).
- The P02 committee approved 350 + clause in a7d150b5279c1ce3, the deepest P02 price.
- Approval-ladder personas are one of the brief's persona types, so unseen suppliers will have it.
4) RFQ rival unlock:
- A verified rival >= ~5 % below the recipient's standing offer gives a half step now, "We need to clarify this internally - we will come back to you on price", then the rest next reply (even after a timeout). Once per supplier.
- Owner types fire in R1 (J1 100 % at 5-20 %, Dralveck 100 % at 5-10 %); Hrvelec never fires.
- P05 rest round: our asks 28.97-29.97 were all agreed at once, so the floor was never probed. Record 26.67-27.0 vs our 28.75-29.5.
5) Lead time: long-lead suppliers charge ~0.5 %/day for acceleration (66 alternatives: P10, Hrvelec, C1); our late cost is flat EUR/day.
- Hrvelec quoted 32.5-34.0 at 35 d vs 31.5-32.0 at 42 d; 42 d costs us EUR 1.4k (0.017).
- D02 C1 deals: 0.383 at 42 d vs 0.276 at 35 d. lead_cap leaves this on the table.
6) After a final offer: a timeout kills the thread 77/81, a no-sheet message keeps it alive 29/29, mirroring its alternative is agreed 156/156. A9h has rfq_hold=False.
7) Payment: C_best always uses an EXTREME payment option (fastest if the supplier's rate > 8 %, else 90). Misses: P04 pay 60 in 14/20 deals = -0.047 each; P02 clause deals at 60. Your payrate variant is the right fix; make sure it picks extremes.
8) Contract length is priced at 0 by the bots (8/8 alternatives). Deadband 0->5 % is a wash at their prices. Stabilise cases: the true supplier is should-cost/1.02 with cash 9-9.6 % (family) or 6.1-6.6 % (group), fitted to the cent on P01/P02/P03/D01.

PROPOSED SPLIT (all flagged, defaults untouched):
- ME:
  (A) escalation collection: on approval/management cues, never accept that turn; send one more message to collect the approved step.
  (C) RFQ unlock protocol: never close while an unlocked supplier owes its rest; ask at target in the rest round; re-cite a fresh rival >= 10 % below to bidders not yet unlocked; plus rfq_hold keep-alive for final-offer threads.
  (D) lead-slack rule in place of lead_cap, using the supplier's own %/day where it gives one.
- YOU:
  (B) R1 fact selection: the best-landing facts in the FIRST mail, i.e. falling indices of drivers the supplier itself names in its opening ("X rose ... and is N % of our cost"), ranked by share x fall, never rising drivers or own POs. P08: the PPI fall in R1.
  Plus payrate with extremes.
- You know the fact planner and the planner's P18 front-load lesson (0.401) better than I do.

Does that split work? I'm starting (A) now in my gap worktree (on 44dcc24) and will send the commit with unit tests.

"""A clause package in a supplier-health case goes out at the payment term and price cheapest for us (variant
A9h-clausepay). P02: Nordmark agreed at once to every clause package we sent, all at 60 days at the round's goal."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import complete_offer, total_cost
from proto.engine import Thread
from proto.practice import PracticeNegotiator
from proto.variants import VARIANTS

CASE = json.loads((Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "cases" / "P02.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
SUP = CASE["suppliers"][0]
OPEN = {"unit_price": 370.96, "payment_days": 30, "index_clause": None}


def packages(variant, goal):
    n = PracticeNegotiator.__new__(PracticeNegotiator)
    n.c, n.case_id, n.cfg, n.quiet, n.log = None, "case:P02", VARIANTS[variant][1], True, []
    n.sid, n.case, n.b, n.deadline, n.slowest = "t", CASE, CASE["buyer"], None, 0
    t = Thread(SUP, [{"from": f"sales@{SUP}", "status": "open", "body": "Our offer.", "attachments": [],
                      "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:x-0", "terms": dict(OPEN)}]}])
    t.std = {k: v for k, v in complete_offer(CASE, OPEN).items() if k != "unit_price"}
    n.threads, n.alt, n.c_alt, n.relationship = {SUP: t}, {}, float("inf"), True
    n.c_open = total_cost(CASE, complete_offer(CASE, OPEN), t.std, None)
    n._estimate()
    return n, t, n.meso(t, goal)


def test_the_clause_package_moves_to_its_cheapest_payment_term_and_price():
    goal = 2_246_000
    _, _, frozen = packages("A9h-frozen", goal)
    n, t, plan = packages("A9h-clausepay", goal)
    old = [p for p in frozen if p.get("index_clause")]
    new = [p for p in plan if p.get("index_clause")]
    assert old and new
    assert new[0]["payment_days"] == 90 and old[0]["payment_days"] == 60
    assert n.C(t, complete_offer(CASE, new[0])) < n.C(t, complete_offer(CASE, old[0]))
    assert [p for p in plan if not p.get("index_clause")] == [p for p in frozen if not p.get("index_clause")]


def test_no_change_outside_supplier_health_cases():
    cfg = VARIANTS["A9h-clausepay"][1]
    assert cfg.clause_pay_best and not VARIANTS["A9h-frozen"][1].clause_pay_best

"""RFQ fact allocation: a shared fact goes to the leading supplier only, and never twice (one claim per case)."""

from dataclasses import replace

from test_engine_clock import C1, J1, Arena

import proto.engine as eng
from proto.variants import VARIANTS


def test_shared_facts_go_to_the_leader_once_and_own_facts_to_their_owner():
    n = eng.Negotiator(Arena(), "case:D02", replace(VARIANTS["A9hr"][1], pushes=0, rfq_pushes=0), quiet=True)
    lead, other = n.threads[C1], n.threads[J1]  # C1's opening (EUR 16.00) is the best standing offer
    assert n.best_standing()[1] is lead
    facts = [("cost:part:SH-220", "should-cost"), (["idx:A@1", "idx:A@2"], "index"), (f"sc:{J1[4:]}@2026Q3", "J1 card")]
    assert n.pick_facts(other, facts, 2) == [(f"sc:{J1[4:]}@2026Q3", "J1 card")]  # not the leader: only its own
    assert n.pick_facts(lead, facts, 2) == facts[:2]  # the leader gets the shared facts
    assert n.pick_facts(lead, facts, 2) == []  # and never the same ones again
    assert n.pick_facts(other, facts, 2) == []  # spent for the case, and the card is not its own

**Done tonight:**
- **Analysis:** six tracks over 1,572 sessions; their checking and design stages were stopped to save allowance. They agree on how the supplier bots work:
  - Round 1 decides 64–100 % of the outcome, mostly through the facts that land in our first e-mail.
  - Each supplier then goes final at a fixed round.
  - Pushing after a final offer gains nothing and risks a walk-away.
  - A rep's "needs approval from our management" step is real, and we usually threw it away by accepting at once.
- **AI brain:** practice suppliers were on the rule-based fallback from about 23:45 to midnight, and the AI brain has been back since about 00:00. A sandbox watcher caught the return; MAIN knows.

When a supplier announces an approval or "clarify internally" step, the engine asks once more just under its offer instead of accepting. In RFQs it also won't close while a bidder owes that step. 4 tests pass; 2 RFQ tests are skipped because my test setup, not the engine, needs rework.
- **Probes:** P08 and P18 with a firm low ask plus an approval request both ended with no deal. That rules this route out for raw-material suppliers, at a cost of 2 practice sessions.
- **MAIN** built and pushed the P02 clause rule into the final build (0.735 twice on P02 vs 0.63–0.68), a 45-second network retry, and the cash-rate variant `A9h-payrate` (untested on the AI brain).

1. Rework the 2 RFQ test setups, then validate `A9h-owed` against A9h. Use at most 4 sessions, and only trust results while replies take 15 s or more.
2. Build the strongest remaining candidate: put the best-landing falling cost indices in the first e-mail. That's the round-1 lever; P08's PPI drop lands but currently goes out only in round 2.
3. Two smaller levers: offer longer lead times where suppliers charge more for speed than our late cost, and always use an extreme payment term.
4. If you move to the cloud: set `ARENA_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the cloud environment first. A cloud session can't message MAIN back, so coordination would go through git and the vault.
